definition_zh: 结合；组合；组合体；密码组合
definition_en: the act of joining two or more things together, or the set of things that results from being joined
core_image: 几块不同的拼图严丝合缝地扣在一起，成了一张完整的画
scene: 厨房里，厨师把几种香料依次撒进锅里。 The combination of spices gave the soup a deep flavour.
sceneCN: 这里 combination 指「结合；组合」（第 1 个义项：把事物合在一起）；句意是几种香料的搭配让汤有了浓郁的味道。

derivatives.zh: 结合；联合
联合的；合并的
可结合的
重组

senses.title: The act of joining
senses.definition: the act of putting two or more things together
senses.definitionCN: 把两样或更多事物放在一起的动作
senses.example: The combination of heat and water slowly softens the beans.
senses.exampleCN: 热与水的共同作用慢慢把豆子煮软。
senses.why: Two things act as one, so the joining itself becomes a thing you can name.
senses.whyCN: 两样东西合为一体，这个「合」的过程本身就成了一件可以命名的事。

senses.title: A set of joined things
senses.definition: a set of different things that are used or seen together
senses.definitionCN: 搭配在一起使用或出现的一组不同事物
senses.example: The room was decorated in a combination of blue and grey.
senses.exampleCN: 房间用蓝灰两色搭配装饰。
senses.why: Once joined, the parts are seen as one whole set rather than separate items.
senses.whyCN: 一旦结合，各部分就被看成一个整体，而不再是一件件单独的东西。

senses.title: Numbers that open a lock
senses.definition: the particular order of numbers or letters needed to open a lock
senses.definitionCN: 打开锁所需要的特定数字或字母顺序
senses.example: He forgot the combination to his bicycle lock.
senses.exampleCN: 他忘了自行车锁的密码。
senses.why: A lock opens only when its numbers are joined in exactly one order.
senses.whyCN: 锁只有在数字按唯一顺序组合起来时才会打开。

intro.en: Combination comes from Latin combinare, which meant to join two things, two by two.
intro.cn: combination 来自拉丁语 combinare，本义是把两样东西成对地并在一起。

items.en: Combinare joined com-, meaning together, with bini, meaning two each.
items.cn: combinare 把表示「一起」的 com- 与意为「各两个」的 bini 合在一起。

items.en: Combinatio named the act of joining things.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 combinatio 指把事物结合起来的动作。

items.en: Old French combinacion carried the word into daily speech.
items.cn: 古法语 combinacion 把这个词带进了日常语言。

items.en: English combination first meant a union of two parties.
items.cn: 英语 combination 最初指两方的联合。

items.en: It spread to spices, colours, teams and the codes of locks.
items.cn: 后来它扩展到香料、颜色、团队以及锁的密码。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that share the shape of combination, while the meaning group names other ways of joining or mixing.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 combination 形似的词，近义组列出其他表示结合与混合的词。

entries.definition: to join two things so that they work together
entries.definitionCN: 把两样东西结合起来

entries.definition: the act of finishing something
entries.definitionCN: 完成；结束

entries.definition: the process of burning
entries.definitionCN: 燃烧的过程

entries.definition: a combination of different substances
entries.definitionCN: 不同物质的混合物

entries.definition: a smooth combination of things
entries.definitionCN: 融合；混合

entries.definition: the joining of two or more groups
entries.definitionCN: 联合；结合

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from the act of joining, then move to the set that results and to the code on a lock.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从结合的动作出发，再走到由此形成的组合与锁上的密码。

normal.en: Com- means together and bini means two each, so the word is built on pairing.
normal.cn: com- 表示一起，bini 表示各两个，这个词天生就在讲配对。

normal.en: A combination lock opens only when its numbers line up in one order.
normal.cn: 密码锁只有在数字按唯一顺序对齐时才会打开。

normal.en: Spices, colours and players all grow stronger as a combination.
normal.cn: 香料、颜色和球员，一旦组合起来都更有力量。

normal.en: Think of a recipe: no single spice, but a combination, gives the taste.
normal.cn: 想想菜谱：让味道成型的不是某一种香料，而是它们的组合。

normal.en: The verb is combine and the noun is combination, one act and one result.
normal.cn: 动词是 combine，名词是 combination，一个是动作，一个是结果。

abstract.en: Picture four puzzle pieces clicking into one picture.
abstract.cn: 想象四块拼图扣在一起，成为一幅画。

abstract.en: Picture a chef tasting the soup and adding one more spice.
abstract.cn: 想象厨师尝一口汤，又添了一味香料。

abstract.en: Picture fingers turning a dial until the lock clicks open.
abstract.cn: 想象手指转动密码盘，直到锁咔哒一声打开。

examples.en: The combination of rain and sun made the garden grow fast.
examples.cn: 雨水与阳光的结合让花园长得很快。

examples.en: Her recipe is a combination of three family dishes.
examples.cn: 她的做法是三道家常菜的融合。

examples.en: Nobody could guess the combination of the safe.
examples.cn: 没人猜得出保险柜的密码。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 combination 记成 com（一起）加 bination：两样东西一起放下，就成了一个组合。

root: 由拉丁语 combinare 而来，com- 表示一起，bini 表示各两个，本义是把两样东西并在一起，后引申为组合体与锁的密码。

sensesIntro.en: From the act of joining, to the set that results, and finally to the code that opens a lock.
sensesIntro.cn: 从结合的动作，到由此形成的组合，再到开锁的密码。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: several pieces fitted so tightly that they work as one.
core.cn: 核心意象：几块不同的拼图严丝合缝地扣在一起，成了一张完整的画。

branches.en: The joining act is the oldest and plainest sense.
branches.cn: 结合的动作是最古老也最朴素的义项。

branches.en: The result of joining is seen as one whole set.
branches.cn: 结合的结果被看成一个整体的组合。

branches.en: A lock code is a combination in the most literal order.
branches.cn: 锁的密码是把数字按最严格的顺序所做的组合。

branches.en: Act and result are two sides of the same joining.
branches.cn: 动作与结果是同一次结合的两面。

branches.en: Spices and numbers both work only in the right combination.
branches.cn: 香料和数字都只有在正确的组合下才起作用。

intro.en: Combination is built from the verb combine plus the noun ending -ation.
intro.cn: combination 由动词 combine 加名词后缀 -ation 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base combinare already carried the idea of pairing two things.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基 combinare 早已含有把两样东西配对的意思。

items.example: The safe has thousands of possible combinations.
items.exampleCN: 这个保险箱有成千上万种可能的密码组合。
这种芯片使用组合逻辑。

items.example: Combine the two lists into one.

items.exampleCN: 她把工作与学习结合起来。
联合起来的队伍轻松获胜。
把颜色搭配好需要练习。

items.meaning: a new combination of existing parts

items.exampleCN: 他在大学研究组合数学。

definition_zh: 难以置信的；不可信的；惊人的；好得离谱的
definition_en: too unlikely or surprising to be believed, or extremely good or extreme
core_image: 听到消息时猛地停住脚步的那一瞬
scene: 球赛最后一秒，替补队员在半场外把球投了出去，全场屏息。 The final shot was simply unbelievable.
sceneCN: 这里 unbelievable 是形容词「难以置信的」（第 2 个义项：因出乎意料而令人惊叹）；句意为最后那一投简直不可思议。

pos.zh: 形容词：难以置信的；不可信的；惊人的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词后缀构成，义为「难以置信地；极其」
同前缀族名词，义为「不信；无信仰」
去掉否定前缀的正面形式，义为「可信的」

senses.title: Too improbable to be believed
senses.definition: so unlikely or inconsistent with fact that it cannot be accepted as true
senses.definitionCN: 因可能性太低或与事实不符而无法被当作真实接受
senses.example: His excuse for missing the exam sounded unbelievable.
senses.exampleCN: 他缺考的理由听起来难以置信。
senses.why: The core image is the mind refusing its grip: the story is offered, the mind will not close around it.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是心智拒绝「握住」：故事递来，心智却不肯合拢。

senses.title: Surprising beyond expectation
senses.definition: so unexpected or extreme that it amazes, as in an unbelievable result
senses.definitionCN: 因出乎意料或极端程度而令人惊叹，如 an unbelievable result
senses.example: The team made an unbelievable comeback in the final minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 球队在最后几分钟上演了不可思议的逆转。
senses.why: The same refusal flips tone: what the mind cannot close around delights instead of offending.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「握不住」换了色调：令人合不拢的不再是谎言，而是惊喜。

senses.title: Extremely good or impressive
senses.definition: very good, often used loosely in speech for emphasis
senses.definitionCN: 非常好，口语中泛用于强调
senses.example: The view from the summit was unbelievable.
senses.exampleCN: 山顶的景色美得让人难以置信。
senses.why: Amazement becomes praise: the word stretches from doubt to delight.
senses.whyCN: 惊叹化为赞美：这个词从怀疑拉伸到欢喜。

senses.title: A price or deal too good or too bad to be real
senses.titleCN: 离谱的价格；可疑的交易
senses.definition: of offers or bargains, so extreme that trust itself is questioned
senses.definitionCN: 就报价或交易而言，极端到令人怀疑其真实性
senses.example: They offered an unbelievable discount on the last day.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一天他们给出了低得离谱的折扣。
senses.why: When an offer outruns belief, the buyer hesitates: is it real, or is it a hook?
senses.whyCN: 当报价超出可信范围，买家便迟疑：是真便宜，还是鱼钩？

senses.title: Unbelievable behaviour
senses.definition: of conduct, so rude, bold or extreme that onlookers are startled
senses.definitionCN: 就行为而言，粗鲁、大胆或极端到令旁观者咋舌
senses.example: His unbelievable rudeness to the waiter shocked the table.
senses.exampleCN: 他对服务生难以置信的无礼震惊了全桌。
senses.why: Social norms are what the mind expects; conduct beyond them will not be taken in.
senses.whyCN: 社会常规是心智的预期；超出预期的举止让人无法「收下」。

senses.title: Unbelievable odds or statistics
senses.definition: of numbers, chances or figures, so far from the normal range that they seem wrong
senses.definitionCN: 就数字、概率或数据而言，偏离正常范围到看似有误
senses.example: She beat odds of a million to one — almost unbelievable.
senses.exampleCN: 她战胜了百万分之一的赔率——几乎令人无法相信。
senses.why: Numbers are checked against expectation; the figure that breaks the scale is unbelievable.
senses.whyCN: 数字要拿预期来校验；打破量程的那个数字便「不可信」。

senses.title: Unbelievable as a stretched exclamation
senses.definition: used alone or in the frame simply unbelievable as an exclamation of amazement
senses.definitionCN: 单独使用或用于 simply unbelievable 框架，作惊叹语
senses.example: They won again? Simply unbelievable!
senses.exampleCN: 他们又赢了？简直难以置信！
senses.why: The adjective hardens into an interjection: the refused belief becomes a cry.
senses.whyCN: 形容词凝固成感叹：被拒绝的「信」化作一声惊呼。

senses.title: Unbelievable weather or conditions
senses.definition: of conditions, so unusual for the place or season that people remark on them
senses.definitionCN: 就天气或境况而言，异于该地该季的常态而引人议论
senses.example: Snow in April here is almost unbelievable.
senses.exampleCN: 这里四月下雪几乎是不可思议的事。
senses.why: Seasons are the world's habit; weather that breaks the habit reads like a tall tale.
senses.whyCN: 季节是世界的习惯；打破习惯的天气读起来像天方夜谭。

intro.en: Unbelievable is un- laid on believable, which itself is believe plus the Latin-derived -able.
intro.cn: unbelievable 是 un- 加 believable，后者本身又是 believe 加源自拉丁语的 -able。

items.en: *leubh- is generally reconstructed as 'to care, desire, love'; the deeper trail is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *leubh- 意为「关爱、渴望、爱」；更早的脉络不确定。

items.en: Proto-Germanic gave *leubon, the ancestor of believe and of love.
items.cn: 原始日耳曼语给出 *leubon，即 believe 与 love 的共同祖先。

items.en: Old English belēavian meant to hold dear, and by extension to hold a thing true.
items.cn: 古英语 belēavian 意为「珍爱」，引申为「把某事当作真实来持有」。

items.en: Believable was formed in the sixteenth century on believe with the suffix -able.
items.cn: 十六世纪在 believe 之上加后缀 -able 构成 believable。

items.en: The negative unbelievable followed, first of tales that could not be credited.
items.cn: 否定式 unbelievable 随之出现，最初指无法取信的故事。

items.en: In the twentieth century the sense stretched to amazed praise, its most common modern use.
items.cn: 二十世纪词义拉伸为惊叹式的赞美，成为现代最常见的用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the believe family; the near-meaning group gathers improbable, incredible and amazing words.
note.cn: 形近组收 believe 词族；近义组收 improbable、incredible 及表惊人的词。

entries.definition: Able to be believed; the positive base of this word.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可信的」，是本词去掉否定前缀的正面形式。

entries.definition: To accept as true; the verb on which the whole family stands.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「相信」，是整个词族的动词基础。

entries.definition: The noun of believing; a thing held true.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「信念；所信之事」。

entries.definition: The lack of belief, especially religious; older sibling of this word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「不信；无信仰」（尤指宗教），是本词的同前缀前辈。

entries.definition: Loved dearly; shares the deep root with believe, since to believe was once to hold dear.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「深爱的」，与 believe 同出深词根，因为「相信」古义即「珍视」。

entries.definition: Impossible or amazing to believe; Latin-built twin of unbelievable.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「难以置信的」，是 unbelievable 的拉丁构词孪生词。

entries.definition: Unlikely to happen or be true; stresses low probability rather than refusal to believe.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不大可能的」，强调概率之低，而非拒绝相信。

entries.definition: Not seeming reasonable or probable; formal, often of stories and excuses.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「难以取信的」，语气正式，多指故事与托辞。

entries.definition: Held in doubt; the doubting stays open rather than refusing.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可疑的；半信半疑的」，怀疑保持开放而非拒绝。

entries.definition: Very surprising; pure amazement without the doubting undertone.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「令人震惊的」，纯表惊叹，不含怀疑底色。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real believe root and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的 believe 词根，以及这个词实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: Un + believable: build the negative on the believe family.
normal.cn: un + believable：在 believe 词族上加否定。

normal.en: Incredible is the Latin twin; unbelievable is the native twin.
normal.cn: incredible 是拉丁构词的孪生词，unbelievable 是本族构词的孪生词。

normal.en: An unbelievable story fails the test of belief.
normal.cn: an unbelievable story 通不过「相信」的检验。

normal.en: Unbelievable luck means luck so good it staggers you.
normal.cn: unbelievable luck 指好到令人瞠目的运气。

normal.en: The root means hold dear: belief is holding a thing dear as true.
normal.cn: 词根本义是「珍视」：相信就是把一件事当真来珍视。

abstract.en: Picture a story offered with open hands; the mind folds its arms and will not take it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个故事被双手奉上，心智却抱臂不接。

abstract.en: Some surprises are refused because the world never promised them.
abstract.cn: 有些惊喜被拒绝，只因世界从未许诺过它们。

abstract.en: When refusal softens, it turns into applause.
abstract.cn: 当拒绝软化，它就变成了喝彩。

examples.en: The ticket cost almost nothing — an unbelievable bargain.
examples.cn: 这张票几乎不要钱——便宜得难以置信。

examples.en: Her recovery after the accident was unbelievable to the doctors.
examples.cn: 她事故后的康复让医生们觉得不可思议。

examples.en: That is simply unbelievable; we closed the deal an hour ago.
examples.cn: 这简直难以置信；我们一小时前才完成交易。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安必离佛」——安必离佛十万八千里，信不得：难以置信

root: unbelievable 由本族否定前缀 un- 加 believable 构成，believable 又由 believe 加拉丁源后缀 -able 构成；believe 经古英语 belēavian 可溯至原始日耳曼语 *leubon 与原始印欧语重构词根 *leubh-「关爱、爱」，与 love 同族。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses of unbelievable all circle one refused grip: tales that cannot be credited, results that amaze, prices that outbid trust, behaviour that startles, odds that break the scale, the hardened exclamation, and weather that breaks the season's habit.
sensesIntro.cn: unbelievable 的八个义项都围绕同一次被拒绝的「握住」：无法取信的故事、令人惊叹的结果、超出信任的报价、令人咋舌的行为、打破量程的赔率、凝固的惊叹语，以及打破季节习惯的天气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the mind's hands are offered something and fold shut instead of closing around it.
core.cn: 核心意象：心智之手被递来一物，却抱臂合拢，不肯握住。

branches.en: THE DOUBT: the story fails the test of belief.
branches.cn: 怀疑线：故事通不过相信的检验。

branches.en: THE AMAZEMENT: the refusal flips into delighted praise.
branches.cn: 惊叹线：拒绝翻转为欣喜的赞美。

branches.en: THE EXCESS: prices, conduct and odds that outrun what the mind can take in.
branches.cn: 超限线：价格、行为与赔率超出心智所能收下。

branches.en: THE CRY: the adjective hardens into an exclamation.
branches.cn: 惊呼线：形容词凝固成一声惊叹。

branches.en: THE SEASON: weather that breaks the world's habit reads like a tale.
branches.cn: 季节线：打破世界习惯的天气读来如同传说。

intro.en: Unbelievable stacks three layers: the native un-, the believe root, and the Latin -able.
intro.cn: unbelievable 叠了三层：本族前缀 un-、believe 词根，以及拉丁源后缀 -able。

latinIntro.en: The root is Germanic and the suffix Latin; only the Indo-European base is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 词根属日耳曼语源，后缀属拉丁语源；只有印欧词基属重构形式。

items.meaning: to hold dear; to hold true
items.example: It is the oldest recorded English step.
items.exampleCN: 它是英语中可考的最早环节。

items.example: It underlies both love and believe.
items.exampleCN: 它同时是 love 与 believe 的底层。
它把 believable 变为 unbelievable。

items.example: It appears in belief, where v becomes f.
items.exampleCN: 它见于 belief，词中 v 变为 f。

items.example: It forms incredible, the Latin twin.
items.exampleCN: 它构成拉丁孪生词 incredible。

items.example: It is the root inside incredible.
items.exampleCN: 它是 incredible 内部的词根。

去掉否定前缀的正面形式，义为「可信的」
同前缀族名词，义为「不信；无信仰」

definition_zh: 转移；转让；换乘；调动；传输；转会
definition_en: to move someone or something from one place, person, or situation to another
core_image: 一只手把杯子里的水倒进另一只杯子：水还是那杯水，位置换了
scene: 银行柜台前，职员核对完信息，提示客户确认汇款：地铁到站广播响起，人群涌出车厢，纷纷快步走向对面站台去换乘、完成自己的 transfer。
sceneCN: 这里 transfer 是动词「换乘」（第 3 个义项：从一地转到另一地）；句意是乘客下车换乘另一条地铁线。

derivatives.zh: 由 transfer 加 -able 构成，义为「可转移的；可转让的」
由 transfer 加 -ence 构成，义为「转移；（心理）移情」
由 transfer 加 -ee 构成，义为「受让人；被调动者」

senses.title: To move something or someone to another place
senses.definition: to take something or someone from one location to another
senses.definitionCN: 把某人某物从一个位置带到另一个位置
senses.example: They transferred the patient to a better hospital.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把病人转到了更好的医院。
senses.why: The core image is pouring water from one cup into another: same thing, new place.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是把水从一杯倒进另一杯：东西不变，位置变了。

senses.title: To hand over rights, money, or property
senses.definition: to legally give rights, money, or property to another person
senses.definitionCN: 依法把权利、钱款或财产交给他人
senses.example: She transferred the house to her daughter.
senses.exampleCN: 她把房子过户给了女儿。
senses.why: Ownership is a thing carried across hands like water.
senses.whyCN: 所有权像水一样被双手「倒」过去。

senses.title: To change from one vehicle or line to another
senses.definition: to change from one bus, train, or flight to another
senses.definitionCN: 换乘另一辆公交、列车或航班
senses.example: Passengers transfer to Line Two at this station.
senses.exampleCN: 乘客在这个站换乘二号线。
senses.why: The passenger himself is the thing carried across.
senses.whyCN: 此刻被「搬运」的正是乘客自己。

senses.title: To move to another job, school, or team
senses.definition: to move a person to another post, school, or club
senses.definitionCN: 把人调动到另一岗位、学校或俱乐部
senses.example: He was transferred to the Shanghai branch last year.
senses.exampleCN: 他去年被调到上海分部。
senses.why: A person's job is poured from one department into another.
senses.whyCN: 一个人的工作被从一个部门「倒」进另一个。

senses.title: To copy information or a disease to something else
senses.definition: to copy data, skills, or a condition onto another thing or person
senses.definitionCN: 把数据、技能或状态复制或传导到另一对象
senses.example: The virus can transfer from animals to humans.
senses.exampleCN: 病毒可以从动物传染给人。
senses.why: What flows across is no longer just things but information and conditions.
senses.whyCN: 跨越的不只是实物，还有信息与状态。

intro.en: Transfer comes from Latin transferre, to carry across, from trans- (across) and ferre (to carry, bear). The noun kept a stressed first syllable, the verb a stressed second.
intro.cn: transfer 来自拉丁语 transferre「搬运过去」，由 trans-（跨越）与 ferre（携带、承担）构成。名词重音在前，动词重音在后。

items.en: transferre meant to carry or bear across.
items.cn: 拉丁语 transferre 意为「搬运过去、带过去」。

items.en: ferre descends from a reconstructed root bher- meaning to carry.
items.cn: ferre 源于重构词根 bher-「携带」（重构形式）。

items.en: In Roman law, transferre covered handing over property.
items.cn: 罗马法中 transferre 用于财产的移转。

items.en: English borrowed the verb through legal and general use.
items.cn: 英语经法律与一般用法借入该动词。

items.en: Now covers money, data, jobs, vehicles, and even emotions.
items.cn: 现代用法涵盖钱款、数据、职务、换乘乃至情感移置。

note.en: Words that look or sound close to transfer, and words in the moving field.
note.cn: 与 transfer 形近音近的词，以及同属转移义场的词。

entries.definition: the act or process of transferring; a psychological term
entries.definitionCN: 转移；移情（心理学术语），transfer 的派生名词

entries.definition: to change the form of
entries.definitionCN: 改造；使变形，同前缀 trans- 不同词根：ferre 搬运，formare 造形

entries.definition: to like one better
entries.definitionCN: 更喜欢，与 transfer 共享拉丁词根 ferre（携带）

entries.definition: to change position
entries.definitionCN: 移动；搬动，泛指位置变化

entries.definition: to change place or direction
entries.definitionCN: 变换；移动，常用于方向与工作

entries.definition: to carry or communicate
entries.definitionCN: 运送；传达，偏正式

entries.definition: to pass along in stages
entries.definitionCN: 接转；传递，强调接力

normalIntro.en: Remember ferre, to carry: transfer always carries something across.
normalIntro.cn: 记住词根 ferre「携带」：transfer 永远是把什么「带过去」。

normal.en: trans- (across) + fer (carry)
normal.cn: trans（跨）+ fer（携带）＝转移过去

normal.en: collocation: transfer money, transfer station
normal.cn: 高频搭配：转账、换乘站

normal.en: transfer vs transform: carry vs shape
normal.cn: transfer 搬运、transform 塑形，前缀相同词根不同

normal.en: noun TRANSfer, verb transFER
normal.cn: 名词重音在前，动词重音在后

normal.en: ferre family: prefer, refer, confer
normal.cn: ferre 词族：prefer、refer、confer

abstract.en: Water poured from one glass into another
abstract.cn: 水从一只杯子倒进另一只杯子

abstract.en: A commuter stepping from one platform to another
abstract.cn: 通勤者从一个站台跨向另一个

abstract.en: A deed of ownership sliding across the desk
abstract.cn: 一纸产权证书滑过桌面

examples.en: Please transfer the money before Friday.
examples.cn: 请在周五前完成转账。

examples.en: She transferred to a high school in Hangzhou.
examples.cn: 她转学到了杭州的一所高中。

examples.en: The embassy arranged the transfer of the prisoner.
examples.cn: 大使馆安排了囚犯的移交。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「踹死佛」——搬家时连佛都踹着走：东西全踹（trans）死（fixed）佛（ferre 携带）→ transfer 什么都能搬走。

root: 拉丁语 trans-（跨越）+ ferre（携带）→ transferre「搬过去」：凡被带过界的，都是 transfer。ferre 同根词还有 prefer、refer、confer。

sensesIntro.en: From carrying things across, the word widened to rights, passengers, jobs, and invisible information.
sensesIntro.cn: 从搬运实物扩展到权利、乘客、职务与无形信息的转移。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water poured from one cup into another
core.cn: 核心意象：水从一杯倒进另一杯

branches.en: things carried to a new location
branches.cn: 被搬到新位置的东西

branches.en: rights and money changing hands
branches.cn: 权利与钱款易主

branches.en: passengers changing vehicles or lines
branches.cn: 乘客换乘交通工具

branches.en: people moved to new posts or schools
branches.cn: 人被调往新岗位或学校

branches.en: even data and diseases travel by the same road
branches.cn: 数据与疾病也走同一条「搬运」之路

intro.en: Transfer is pure Latin: the prefix trans- on the irregular verb ferre.
intro.cn: transfer 是纯拉丁构词：不规则动词 ferre 加前缀 trans-。

latinIntro.en: Latin ferre also gave offer, refer, suffer, confer, and differ.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ferre 还派生了 offer、refer、suffer、confer 与 differ。

items.meaning: to carry back to a source

definition_zh: 相关的；切题的
definition_en: closely connected with the subject being discussed; useful and important for a particular purpose
core_image: 一叠材料里只有几页被抽出来放到桌子中央
scene: 一叠厚厚的材料摊在桌上，他从中抽出几页，放到桌子中央。 Only the facts relevant to the case were read aloud.
sceneCN: 这里 relevant 是「相关的」（第 1 个义项：与正在讨论的问题直接有关）；句意为只有与本案相关的事实被朗读出来。画面里可留意：被抽出的几页、桌子中央。

derivatives.zh: 相关性；切题
相关地
不相关的

senses.title: Connected with the matter
senses.definition: directly connected with the subject or the problem at hand
senses.definitionCN: 与手头的话题或问题直接相连
senses.example: Only the facts relevant to the case were read aloud.
senses.exampleCN: 只有与本案相关的事实被朗读出来。
senses.why: The word began as a picture of something lifted up to help, and it now names whatever lifts a discussion forward.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初描绘被举起以提供帮助之物，如今命名一切能推动讨论向前的东西。

senses.title: Useful and to the point
senses.definition: important and useful for the purpose being considered
senses.definitionCN: 对正在考虑的目的而言重要且有用
senses.example: Her question was short but highly relevant to the decision.
senses.exampleCN: 她的问题很短，却与这项决定高度相关。
senses.why: Connection alone is not enough; the thing must also carry weight, which is why relevant often implies useful.
senses.whyCN: 仅有联系还不够，那件事物还必须具有分量，因此 relevant 常隐含「有用」。

intro.en: Relevant comes from a Latin verb meaning to lift up and relieve, not from the carrying verb behind relate; the two families are distinct.
intro.cn: relevant 出自一个意为「举起、减轻」的拉丁动词，而不是 relate 所属的那个「携带」动词；这两个词族彼此不同。

items.en: Levare meant to lift up or make light, built on levis, light in weight.
items.cn: levare 意为举起或使轻，由 levis（轻的）构成。

items.en: Relevare joined re- with levare and meant to raise up, relieve, or assist.
items.cn: relevare 由 re- 与 levare 组合，意为举起、减轻或援助。

items.en: The participle relevans, lifting up or helping, named what comes to the aid of a matter.
items.cn: 分词 relevans（举起或帮助）指对某件事物施以援手者。

items.en: French relevant meant depending upon or pertinent, and English took the adjective in that sense.
items.cn: 法语 relevant 意为「取决于」或「切题」，英语即以这个意义借入形容词。

items.en: English narrowed the word to what bears on the question under discussion.
items.cn: 英语把这个词收窄为「与正在讨论的问题有关」。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that resemble relevant; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of pertinence.
note.cn: 形近组收与 relevant 形近的词；近义组收表示切题的形容词。

entries.definition: The quality of being relevant.
entries.definitionCN: 相关性；切题。

entries.definition: Not connected with the matter.
entries.definitionCN: 不相关的。

entries.definition: Depending on something.
entries.definitionCN: 依赖的。

entries.definition: Directly relevant to the matter.
entries.definitionCN: 相关的；切题的。

entries.definition: Able to be applied to a case.
entries.definitionCN: 适用的。

entries.definition: Relevant and appropriate.
entries.definitionCN: 贴切的；有关的。

entries.definition: Connected or associated.
entries.definitionCN: 相关的。

normalIntro.en: The word points to what is lifted up to help the discussion: not everything connected, only what carries weight.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词指向被举起来帮助讨论的东西：不是所有有关联的，而是有分量的那些。

normal.en: Relevant to means it bears on the question.
normal.cn: relevant to 指它压在正在讨论的问题上。

normal.en: Relevant experience is experience that helps this job.
normal.cn: relevant experience 是对这份工作有用的经验。

normal.en: The opposite is irrelevant, the prefix marking the absence.
normal.cn: 反义词是 irrelevant，前缀标记「没有」。

normal.en: The noun is relevance, the quality of fitting the matter.
normal.cn: 名词是 relevance，即切合这件事的性质。

normal.en: Relevant is not from relate, though the two look alike.
normal.cn: relevant 并非出自 relate，尽管两者形似。

abstract.en: A fact is not relevant in itself; it is relevant to a question.
abstract.cn: 事实本身并无相关性，它只相对于某个问题才相关。

abstract.en: To stay relevant is to keep answering questions people still ask.
abstract.cn: 保持切题，就是持续回答人们仍在问的问题。

abstract.en: The skill of thinking is largely the skill of discarding what is irrelevant.
abstract.cn: 思考的本领，很大程度上是丢掉无关之物的本领。

examples.en: Only the facts relevant to the case were read aloud.
examples.cn: 只有与本案相关的事实被朗读出来。

examples.en: Her question was short but highly relevant to the decision.
examples.cn: 她的问题很短，却与这项决定高度相关。

examples.en: He listed the skills relevant to the job in one short paragraph.
examples.cn: 他用一小段话列出了与这份工作相关的技能。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（往回、向上）加 lev（举起）加 ant：被举到讨论中央、能撑起这个问题的，就是「相关的、切题的」。

root: 拉丁 levis（轻的）→ levare（举起、使轻）→ relevare（举起、减轻、援助）→ relevans（帮助的）→ 法语 relevant → 英语 relevant；出自 lev- 词族，与 relate/relation 的 referre 词族不同源。同族有 relevance、irrelevant。

sensesIntro.en: The core is what bears on the matter; the senses move from a direct connection to usefulness and weight.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「压在议题上」；义项从直接的联系，到有用与有分量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a few pages pulled out of a thick file and set in the middle of the table.
core.cn: 核心意象：一叠材料里只有几页被抽出来放到桌子中央。

branches.en: facts tied to one case
branches.cn: 与一个案件相连的事实

branches.en: a short question that decides
branches.cn: 一个决定走向的短问题

branches.en: connected and also weighty
branches.cn: 既相连又有分量

branches.en: a paragraph that answers the advert
branches.cn: 回答了招聘要求的一段话

branches.en: a page kept and a page set aside
branches.cn: 留下的一页与放到一边的一页

intro.en: A Latin verb of lifting becomes a participle of helping, and the participle names what is worth bringing into a discussion.
intro.cn: 拉丁语表「举起」的动词变成表「帮助」的分词，这个分词便命名值得被带进讨论的东西。

latinIntro.en: The base is levare, to lift, from levis, light; re- adds force, and -ant forms the adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是 levare（举起），出自 levis（轻的）；re- 加强语气，-ant 构成形容词。

definition_zh: 视觉的、看得见的；直观展示的图像
definition_en: relating to seeing or the eyes; a picture or display used to show something
core_image: 投影仪亮起：白墙上出现所有人都看得见的画面
scene: 会议室灯光暗下，白墙亮起第一张图表。 The report uses strong visuals to explain the data.
sceneCN: 这里 visual 是「视觉展示物」（第 3 个义项：用来说明的图像）；句意为报告用醒目的图像来解释数据。灯光下人人都看得见的画面，就是这个词。

pos.zh: 形容词：视觉的；看得见的
名词：视觉资料、图像展示

derivatives.zh: 副词，义为「在视觉上」，由形容词加 -ly 构成
名词，义为「视力、想象」，同根名词
动词，义为「使形象化、想象」，由 visual 加 -ize 构成
形容词，义为「视听的」，由 audio- 加 visual 构成

senses.title: Of the eyes
senses.titleCN: 视觉的：与看和眼睛相关
senses.definition: connected with seeing or with the eyes
senses.definitionCN: 与观看或眼睛有关
senses.example: Reading is a visual skill learned step by step.
senses.exampleCN: 阅读是一种逐步习得的视觉技能。
senses.why: The adjective pins the whole act of seeing onto the noun it modifies.
senses.whyCN: 形容词把「看」这一行为整体固定到所修饰的名词上。

senses.title: Able to be seen
senses.definition: visible or able to be noticed by the eye
senses.definitionCN: 可见的、能被眼睛察觉的
senses.example: The crack shows a visual sign of the building's age.
senses.exampleCN: 裂缝是这座建筑年代的肉眼可见的迹象。
senses.why: What exists for the eye exists plainly; sight is the proof.
senses.whyCN: 对眼睛而言存在的东西确凿可见，看见即证明。

senses.title: A picture used to show
senses.titleCN: 图像：用来说明的视觉展示物
senses.definition: a picture, chart, or display used to explain or present something
senses.definitionCN: 用于解释或展示的图画、图表或演示
senses.example: The report uses strong visuals to explain the data.
senses.exampleCN: 报告用醒目的图像来解释数据。
senses.why: The adjective steps forward as a noun: the thing meant for the eye.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转作名词：专供眼睛看的东西。

senses.title: Of optical devices
senses.titleCN: 光学装置的：帮助看的仪器
senses.definition: of instruments that help or extend the eye, such as lenses
senses.definitionCN: 属于帮助或延伸眼睛的仪器，如镜片
senses.example: The patient chose new visual aids last week.
senses.exampleCN: 病人上周选配了新的助视器。
senses.why: The eye gains tools; the word labels anything that serves sight.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛有了工具，这个词标示一切服务于视觉的器械。

intro.en: Visual is the adjective of the Latin see-root videre, built with the suffix -ual.
intro.cn: visual 是拉丁「看」词根 videre 的形容词形式，由后缀 -ual 构成。

items.en: The reconstructed root *weid- means to see or to know.
items.cn: 重构词根 *weid- 意为看或知晓。

items.en: Videre means to see; the adjective visualis means of sight or seeing.
items.cn: 拉丁语 videre 意为看；形容词 visualis 意为视觉的。

items.en: Visualis appears in late philosophical Latin, distinguishing knowledge from sight.
items.cn: visualis 出现在晚期哲学拉丁语中，用以区分认知与视觉。

items.en: English borrows visual as a term of optics and anatomy before it becomes everyday.
items.cn: 英语先在光学与解剖学语境借用 visual，后转为日常用词。

items.en: The noun use for pictures in media and talks is a twentieth-century development.
items.cn: 指代媒体与演讲中图片的名词用法是二十世纪的发展。

note.en: Look-alikes share the see-root; near meanings cover the visible world and its pictures.
note.cn: 形近组共享「看」词根，近义组涵盖可见世界及其图像。

entries.definition: the ability to see or an imagined picture
entries.definitionCN: 视力、想象；visual 的同根名词

entries.definition: to form a picture in the mind
entries.definitionCN: 使形象化、想象；visual 加 -ize 构成

entries.definition: relaxed and informal
entries.definitionCN: 随意的；与 visual 拼写尾段相近，词根为拉丁 casus（偶然），不同源

entries.definition: happening in the ordinary way
entries.definitionCN: 通常的；词根为拉丁 usus（使用），与 visual 词源不同，仅拼写相近

entries.definition: a face or appearance
entries.definitionCN: 面容；同出「看」词族的文学用词

entries.definition: able to be seen
entries.definitionCN: 可见的；与看得见义相邻，visible 强调状态，visual 强调领域

entries.definition: relating to light and vision, especially instruments
entries.definitionCN: 光学的；与光学装置义相邻

entries.definition: of drawing or pictures that show information
entries.definitionCN: 图示的；与图像义相邻，偏绘制

entries.definition: shown in pictures
entries.definitionCN: 图片的；与图像义相邻，偏叙事图画

entries.definition: of the eye itself, formal or medical
entries.definitionCN: 眼睛的，正式或医学用语

normalIntro.en: Five anchors from the adjective of the see-root.
normalIntro.cn: 五个锚点，来自「看」词根的形容词。

normal.en: visual is what belongs to the eyes.
normal.cn: visual 属于眼睛。

normal.en: audiovisual pairs sound with sight in one word.
normal.cn: audiovisual 把声音与视觉放进一个词。

normal.en: visual arts are the arts you look at, like painting and film.
normal.cn: 视觉艺术是供观看的艺术，如绘画与电影。

normal.en: visualize means to make an inner picture, adding -ize to visual.
normal.cn: visualize 是在脑中成像，由 visual 加 -ize 构成。

normal.en: visually compares with verbally: by eye versus by word.
normal.cn: visually 与 verbally 相对：靠眼看与靠话讲。

abstract.en: A beam of light from a projector: everything it touches becomes visual.
abstract.cn: 投影仪的一束光：它照到哪里，哪里就变成视觉的。

abstract.en: Eyes open, the world arrives; eyes closed, only the inner picture remains.
abstract.cn: 睁眼世界到来，闭眼只剩内心的画面。

abstract.en: A chart on white paper: numbers turned into something the eye can grasp.
abstract.cn: 白纸上的图表：数字变成了眼睛能抓住的东西。

examples.en: The teacher added a visual to every hard concept.
examples.cn: 老师为每个难点概念都配了一幅图示。

examples.en: Noise pollution is invisible, but light pollution has clear visual effects.
examples.cn: 噪声污染不可见，而光污染有清晰的视觉影响。

examples.en: The film relies on visual storytelling rather than dialogue.
examples.cn: 这部电影依靠视觉叙事而非对白。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂小姐」——喂给眼睛看的小姐就是「视觉的」画面；谐音只是记忆钩子，词源来自拉丁 visualis（视觉的）。

root: 拉丁语 videre（看）→ visualis（视觉的）→ 英语 visual。同根词 vision、view、evident；形容词后缀 -ual 表示「与……相关」。

sensesIntro.en: The adjective of seeing spreads from the eyes to the visible, then to the pictures made for the eye.
sensesIntro.cn: 「看」的形容词从眼睛铺向可见之物，再到专供眼睛的图像。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: everything that belongs to the eye
core.cn: 核心意象：一切属于眼睛的东西

branches.en: The eye and its skill, like reading
branches.cn: 眼睛及其技能，如阅读

branches.en: What the eye can catch in the world
branches.cn: 世界中眼睛能捕捉的：可见之物

branches.en: Pictures made for eyes, charts and screens
branches.cn: 专为眼睛制作的图像、图表与屏幕

branches.en: Tools that carry sight further, lenses and aids
branches.cn: 延伸视线的工具：镜片与助视器

branches.en: Shared displays let many eyes see one thing
branches.cn: 共享的展示让许多眼睛看同一件事

intro.cn: 「看」词根加上各种前后缀，构成形容词、动词与名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin visualis already had the modern shape of the word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 visualis 已具备这个词的现代形态。

definition_zh: 伤害；损伤；（感情或名誉的）损害
definition_en: harm done to a person's body, feelings, or reputation, often as the result of an accident
core_image: 身体或名誉上留下的那道伤口
scene: 球场边，队医打开急救箱为倒地球员处理膝盖。 The doctor bandaged the injury on his knee quickly.
sceneCN: 这里 injury 是「损伤」（第 1 个义项：身体上的伤口或损害）；句意：队医迅速包扎了他膝盖上的伤处。

derivatives.zh: 同根动词，义为「使受伤；伤害」
由名词加形容词后缀构成，义为「有害的」

senses.title: Physical harm to the body
senses.definition: damage to part of the body caused by an accident or attack
senses.definitionCN: 因事故或攻击造成的身体部位损害
senses.example: The crash left her with a back injury.
senses.exampleCN: 车祸使她的背部受了伤。
senses.why: The Latin root means wrong, and an injury is the wrong done to a body made visible.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「不义」，injury 就是被具体呈现出来的身体之「伤」。

senses.title: Emotional or reputational harm
senses.definition: hurt done to feelings, pride, or a good name
senses.definitionCN: 对感情、自尊或名誉造成的伤害
senses.example: The rumor did real injury to her standing in the team.
senses.exampleCN: 谣言确实损害了她在队中的地位。
senses.why: Invisible wounds are named with the same word as visible ones.
senses.whyCN: 无形的伤与有形的伤共用同一个词。

senses.title: In law, harm giving right to compensation
senses.definition: in legal use, harm for which compensation can be claimed
senses.definitionCN: 法律上可要求赔偿的损害
senses.example: He claimed damages for the personal injury.
senses.exampleCN: 他就人身伤害提出了赔偿要求。
senses.why: The word's legal ancestry remains alive in courtroom usage.
senses.whyCN: 该词的法律血统在法庭用语中依然鲜活。

intro.en: Injury descends from the Latin noun iniuria, meaning wrong or injustice.
intro.cn: injury 由拉丁名词 iniuria（不义、侵害）一脉相承。

items.en: Latin iniuria meant wrong, injustice, from in- (not) plus ius (law, right).
items.cn: 拉丁语 iniuria 意为「不义、侵害」，由 in-（不）加 ius（法、正当）构成。

items.en: Anglo-Norman used injurie in legal texts about wrongful harm.
items.cn: 盎格鲁-诺曼法语在法律文书中用 injurie 指不法侵害。

items.en: English took injury in the fourteenth century, still close to its legal sense.
items.cn: 英语十四世纪引入 injury，仍贴近其法律义。

items.en: The physical-wound sense strengthened from the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 十六世纪起身体创伤义逐渐增强。

items.en: Today medicine, sport, and law are the word's three main homes.
items.cn: 如今医学、体育与法律是该词的三大主要领域。

note.en: Look-alikes share the law-root; near-meaning nouns differ in severity and register.
note.cn: 形近词共享「法」词根；近义名词在严重程度与语体上有别。

entries.definition: to cause injury
entries.definitionCN: 使受伤；injury 的动词

entries.definition: harmful
entries.definitionCN: 有害的；书面语

entries.definition: unfairness
entries.definitionCN: 不公正；同根词，来自 ius

entries.definition: an open injury, especially by a weapon
entries.definitionCN: （开放性）创伤；多指武器所致

entries.definition: harm reducing value or function
entries.definitionCN: 损害；强调价值或功能受损

entries.definition: pain or harm, everyday register
entries.definitionCN: 伤痛；日常用词

normalIntro.en: Five links built from the real root and word family.
normalIntro.cn: 五条基于真实词根与词族的联想。

normal.en: in- (not) + ius (law): iniuria, the wrong that breaks right.
normal.cn: in-（不）+ ius（法）：iniuria，破坏「正当」的错。

normal.en: Verb and noun pair: injure the act, injury the wound.
normal.cn: 动名配对：injure 是动作，injury 是伤口。

normal.en: Idiom: add insult to injury, one hurt piled on another.
normal.cn: 习语：add insult to injury，伤上再加辱。

normal.en: Football fans know injury time, added for stoppages.
normal.cn: 球迷熟知 injury time，因伤停而补时。

normal.en: Legal side: personal injury claims.
normal.cn: 法律层面：人身伤害索赔。

abstract.en: A white bandage wrapped around a knee.
abstract.cn: 白色的绷带缠在膝盖上。

abstract.en: An X-ray film held up to the light.
abstract.cn: X 光片被举到灯前。

abstract.en: A courtroom folder marked compensation.
abstract.cn: 法庭上标注赔偿的文件夹。

examples.en: The striker returned to the team after a long injury.
examples.cn: 这位前锋长期伤停后重返球队。

examples.en: Adding insult to injury, the referee blamed the victim.
examples.cn: 更糟的是，裁判反而责怪了受害者。

examples.en: The court awarded money for his injuries.
examples.cn: 法院就他的伤情判给了赔偿金。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因啾瑞」——受伤后因疼「啾啾」叫，需要「瑞」士急救包。

root: 拉丁语 iniuria（不义、侵害），由 in-（不）加 ius（法、正当）构成；经法语 injurie 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: One wound-word serves the body, the heart, and the courtroom.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个「伤」字同时服务于身体、内心与法庭。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the wound left behind
core.cn: 核心意象：留下的那道伤

branches.en: bodies damaged in accidents
branches.cn: 事故中受损的身体

branches.en: feelings and reputations bruised
branches.cn: 受挫的感情与名誉

branches.en: harm that earns compensation
branches.cn: 可获赔偿的损害

branches.en: bodily harm measured in court
branches.cn: 在法庭上被计量的身体伤害

branches.en: the same wound-word for skin and soul
branches.cn: 皮肉与灵魂共用的伤字

intro.cn: 构词短小：前缀加「法」词根加后缀。

latinIntro.en: Ius again shows its legal family strength.
latinIntro.cn: ius 再次展现其法律词族的实力。

definition_zh: 泥；烂泥；泥浆；泥料；淤泥；污名
definition_en: wet soft earth, the same material used for building, fine sediment in water and, figuratively, dirt thrown at a reputation
core_image: 雨后路上被车轮碾出的两道深沟，泥水顺着沟沿往外渗
scene: 雨下了一夜，村口的土路被车轮碾出两道深沟。 The truck's wheels sank deep into the mud.
sceneCN: 这里是「泥、烂泥」（第 1 个义项：湿软的泥土）；句意为卡车的轮子深陷泥中。图中可辨识物件：土路、车辙、车轮。

pos.zh: 泥；烂泥；泥浆；泥料；淤泥；污名

collocations.zh: 泥饼（儿童用泥做的假饼）

derivatives.zh: 由 mud 加 -y 构成，义为「泥泞的」；作动词指「使浑浊」
由 mud 与 guard 复合而成，义为「挡泥板」
由 mud 与 flat 复合而成，义为「潮间带的泥滩」
由 mud 与 slinging 复合而成，义为「竞选中的抹黑攻击」

senses.title: Wet, soft earth
senses.definition: soft wet earth that sticks to shoes and wheels
senses.definitionCN: 湿软、会粘在鞋和车轮上的泥土
senses.example: The truck's wheels sank deep into the mud.
senses.exampleCN: 卡车的轮子深陷泥中。
senses.why: The Germanic word names the soft, sticky ground itself, so the physical sensation of sticking is the centre of the meaning.
senses.whyCN: 这个日耳曼词指的就是那种软而黏的地面本身，所以「黏住」的身体感觉是词义的中心。

senses.title: Earth and water used as building material
senses.definition: clay or earth mixed with water and shaped or spread while wet
senses.definitionCN: 黏土或泥土加水调成，趁湿塑形或涂抹的材料
senses.example: The old walls were built of mud and straw.
senses.exampleCN: 那些老墙是用泥和草茎砌成的。
senses.why: If mud is soft ground, it can also be handled and shaped, so the same word names the raw material of a wall.
senses.whyCN: 既然泥是软的地面，它也能被捧起来塑形，于是同一个词又指砌墙的原料。

senses.title: Fine sediment at the bottom of water
senses.definition: fine particles that settle on the bed of a river, lake or sea
senses.definitionCN: 沉在河、湖或海底的细小颗粒
senses.example: The river bed was covered with thick black mud.
senses.exampleCN: 河床上覆盖着厚厚的黑泥。
senses.why: Mud carried by water eventually settles, and the settled layer keeps the name of the wet earth that made it.
senses.whyCN: 被水带走的泥终究会沉下来，沉积的那一层仍沿用形成它的湿土之名。

senses.title: A reputation dirtied in public
senses.definition: used in phrases such as drag someone's name through the mud to mean public accusation and disgrace
senses.definitionCN: 用于「drag someone's name through the mud」一类说法，指公开指责与名誉受损
senses.example: The scandal dragged his name through the mud.
senses.exampleCN: 那桩丑闻把他的名声拖进泥里。
senses.why: Being covered in mud is visible and humiliating, so the image transfers neatly to a reputation covered in public accusation.
senses.whyCN: 浑身沾泥既显眼又难堪，于是这个画面很自然地转到被公开指责覆盖的名声上。

intro.en: Mud is a Germanic word for soft wet earth, probably reaching English from Low German, and it has no reliable Latin relative.
intro.cn: mud 是日耳曼语中表示湿软泥土的词，可能经低地德语进入英语，它没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

items.en: A reconstructed stem often written mud- is generally thought to underlie the Germanic words for wet earth, though its exact shape is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为，一个常写作 mud- 的日耳曼语重构词干是各语言表示湿土的词的底子，但其确切形式并不确定。

items.en: Low German mudde is the form most often cited as the immediate source of the English word.
items.cn: 低地德语 mudde 是最常被引为英语这个词直接来源的形式。

items.en: Middle English mudde appeared in the thirteenth century for soft wet ground and for the mire of streets.
items.cn: 中古英语 mudde 在十三世纪出现，指湿软的地面，也指街道上的泥泞。

items.en: The spelling settled as mud, and the word spread to building material and to river sediment.
items.cn: 拼写定型为 mud，词义也扩展到建筑材料与河底沉积物。

items.en: Modern English mud keeps the literal ground sense and supplies the image behind phrases about ruined reputations.
items.cn: 现代英语的 mud 保留字面的泥土义，并为关于名誉受损的短语提供画面。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms built on the mud stem, while the near-meaning group collects other words for soft wet ground and sediment.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在 mud 词干上的形式，近义组收其他表示湿软地面与沉积物的词。

entries.definition: Covered with mud, or to make something unclear.
entries.definitionCN: 沾满泥的，或使某物变得浑浊。

entries.definition: A cover that keeps mud off a wheel.
entries.definitionCN: 挡住车轮泥水的护板。

entries.definition: Low muddy ground left bare by the tide.
entries.definitionCN: 退潮后露出的低洼泥地。

entries.definition: The practice of attacking a rival's reputation in public.
entries.definitionCN: 公开攻击对手名声的做法。

entries.definition: A thin, slippery, unpleasant wet substance.
entries.definitionCN: 稀薄、湿滑而令人不适的物质。

entries.definition: Fine earth carried by water and left as sediment.
entries.definitionCN: 被水带来并沉积下来的细土。

entries.definition: Heavy, sticky earth that can be shaped when wet.
entries.definitionCN: 湿时可塑形的厚重黏土。

entries.definition: Thick, soft, dirty material, often industrial waste.
entries.definitionCN: 浓稠、柔软而肮脏的物质，常指工业废泥。

normalIntro.en: The word names the soft ground itself, and its family keeps adding things to it or moving it with water.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词指的就是那种软的地面本身，同族词则不断给它加东西，或让它随水流动。

normal.en: Mud probably came into English from Low German mudde, which is why its shape is so short and plain.
normal.cn: mud 很可能从低地德语 mudde 进入英语，所以它的词形才如此短而朴素。

normal.en: muddy adds -y to mud: full of mud, therefore unclear and stained.
normal.cn: muddy 在 mud 后加 -y，意为「满是泥的」，因此也指浑浊与沾污。

normal.en: mudguard and mudflat are compounds: one stops mud, the other names ground the tide leaves bare.
normal.cn: mudguard 与 mudflat 都是复合词：一个挡住泥，一个指潮水退后露出的泥地。

normal.en: Mud is uncountable, so one says a lot of mud rather than many muds.
normal.cn: mud 不可数，所以说 a lot of mud，而不说 many muds。

normal.en: The phrase drag a name through the mud turns the visible stain of earth into a public stain on honour.
normal.cn: 「drag a name through the mud」这个说法把泥土可见的污迹变成名誉上公开的污点。

abstract.en: Mud is what water does to solid ground when it stays too long.
abstract.cn: 泥是水在实地上停留太久之后做出来的东西。

abstract.en: Every footprint is mud remembering the shape of a shoe for a little while.
abstract.cn: 每个脚印都是泥暂时记住一只鞋的形状。

abstract.en: The same stuff that builds a wall can also dirty a name.
abstract.cn: 砌得起墙的东西，也能弄脏一个名字。

examples.en: The truck's wheels sank deep into the mud.
examples.cn: 卡车的轮子深陷泥中。

examples.en: Rain turned the path into a river of mud.
examples.cn: 雨水把小路变成了一条泥河。

examples.en: The children built castles out of mud.
examples.cn: 孩子们用泥堆起了城堡。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马的」——马的在泥里踩出一串深坑；记住 mud 是泥。

root: 中古英语 mudde 可能来自低地德语 mudde，指湿软的泥土；一般认为与日耳曼语表示湿土的词干有关，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is wet soft earth; the senses then divide into building material, river sediment, and the figurative stain on a reputation.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是湿软的泥土；义项由此分出建筑材料、河底沉积物，以及名誉上的比喻性污迹。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two deep wheel ruts in a village road after a night of rain.
core.cn: 核心意象：下了一夜雨，村口土路上被车轮碾出的两道深辙。

branches.en: boots pulling free of a wet path
branches.cn: 靴子从湿路上拔出来

branches.en: hands shaping a wall from wet earth
branches.cn: 用手把湿土糊成墙

branches.en: a river bed layered with dark silt
branches.cn: 河床积着黑色的淤泥

branches.en: a headline that soils a reputation
branches.cn: 一条把名声弄脏的标题

branches.en: mud on a shoe and mud on a name
branches.cn: 鞋上的泥与名声上的泥

intro.en: The word is a short Germanic noun of wet earth, with an adjective ending and several compounds built on top of it.
intro.cn: 这个词是日耳曼语中表示湿土的短名词，在它上面还长出一个形容词词尾和几个复合形式。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word, so the Latin side is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录，因此拉丁语部分留空。

definition_zh: 加强；巩固；增强
definition_en: to make something stronger, more solid, or more effective
core_image: 在一根柱子上再加一道支撑，让它更稳
scene: 锻炼能增强肌肉。 Exercise can strengthen your muscles.
sceneCN: 这里 strengthen 是「增强」（第 1 个义项）；句意：锻炼能增强肌肉。

derivatives.zh: 力量
强壮的
强化

senses.title: Make physically stronger
senses.definition: to make a body, structure, or material stronger
senses.definitionCN: 使身体、结构或材料更强
senses.example: Exercise can strengthen your muscles.
senses.exampleCN: 锻炼能增强肌肉。
senses.why: This is added power in the body.
senses.whyCN: 这是给身体增加力量。

senses.title: Make a bond firmer
senses.definition: to make a relationship, position, or system more secure
senses.definitionCN: 使关系、地位或体系更稳固
senses.example: The visit strengthened ties between the two cities.
senses.exampleCN: 这次访问加强了两座城市之间的联系。
senses.why: Bonds can be braced like beams.
senses.whyCN: 关系也能像梁一样被加固。

senses.title: Make more convincing
senses.definition: to make an argument, feeling, or effect stronger
senses.definitionCN: 使论点、感受或效果更有力
senses.example: The new evidence strengthened her case.
senses.exampleCN: 新证据使她的论据更有力。
senses.why: A case stands like a structure and can be braced.
senses.whyCN: 论据像建筑一样立着，也能被加固。

intro.en: Strengthen is strength plus the verb ending -en.
intro.cn: strengthen 由 strength 加动词后缀 -en 构成。

items.en: Strengþu named power.
items.cn: strengþu 指力量。

items.en: Strengthen meant to give strength.
items.cn: 中古英语 strengthen 意为赋予力量。

items.en: It described making the body stronger.
items.cn: 它用来描写让身体更强壮。

items.en: It spread to buildings and systems.
items.cn: 词义扩展到建筑与制度。

items.en: It also came to mean making a case stronger.
items.cn: 也表示让论据更有力。

note.en: Strengthen is compared with look-alike words and with words for making stronger.
note.cn: 把 strengthen 与形近词以及表示加强的词作比较。

entries.definition: power
entries.definitionCN: 力量

entries.definition: the measure from end to end
entries.definitionCN: 长度

entries.definition: needing great effort
entries.definitionCN: 费力的

entries.definition: to make stronger with support
entries.definitionCN: 加固

entries.definition: to increase or improve
entries.definitionCN: 提升

entries.definition: to make hard or firm
entries.definitionCN: 使变硬

normalIntro.en: Strengthen is the act of adding strength to something already standing.
normalIntro.cn: strengthen 是给已经立着的东西再加一份力量。

normal.en: Walking strengthens the legs.
normal.cn: 走路能让双腿更有力。

normal.en: The two countries strengthened their ties.
normal.cn: 两国加强了联系。

normal.en: A second lock strengthened the door.
normal.cn: 第二把锁让门更牢固。

normal.en: The news strengthened her resolve.
normal.cn: 这个消息增强了她的决心。

normal.en: They strengthened the bridge with steel.
normal.cn: 他们用钢材加固了桥梁。

abstract.en: To strengthen is to help something hold its ground.
abstract.cn: 加强，就是帮某物站稳。

abstract.en: Bonds grow stronger by being used.
abstract.cn: 关系越用越牢固。

abstract.en: A brave choice strengthens the one who makes it.
abstract.cn: 勇敢的选择，会让做出选择的人更强。

examples.en: Exercise can strengthen your muscles.
examples.cn: 锻炼能增强肌肉。

examples.en: The visit strengthened ties between the two cities.
examples.cn: 这次访问加强了两座城市之间的联系。

examples.en: The new evidence strengthened her case.
examples.cn: 新证据使她的论据更有力。

dict_mnemonic.text: strengthen 是 strength 加 -en，也就是「使有力量」；肌肉变强是增强，关系变牢是巩固，论据变硬是更有力。

root: 由 strength（力量）加动词后缀 -en 构成；从给身体增加力量，扩展到加固结构与关系，再用于增强论据、信心与效果。

sensesIntro.en: Strengthen adds power to a body, firmness to a bond, and weight to an argument.
sensesIntro.cn: strengthen 给身体加力量，给关系加牢固，给论据加分量。

core.en: A second beam braced against the first.
core.cn: 第二根梁撑住第一根。

branches.en: A runner adds one more hill.
branches.cn: 跑者多跑一个坡。

branches.en: Two towns sign a new agreement.
branches.cn: 两座城镇签下新协议。

branches.en: A document supports the claim.
branches.cn: 一份文件支撑了主张。

branches.en: Practice strengthens both body and trust.
branches.cn: 练习既强身体，也强信任。

branches.en: Proof strengthens a promise between people.
branches.cn: 证据让人与人之间的承诺更稳。

intro.en: Strengthen takes verb endings and is built on strength.
intro.cn: strengthen 加动词词尾，其基础是 strength。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.meaning: to make a standing more secure
items.exampleCN: 这场胜利巩固了他的地位。

definition_zh: 恐怖；恐惧；反恐
definition_en: a very strong feeling of fear, or the use of fear to control people
core_image: 黑暗里突然攥紧心脏的那只手
scene: 爆炸发生后全城戒备。 The city lived in terror for weeks.
sceneCN: 这里 terror 是「恐怖」（第 2 个义项）；句意：全城在恐怖中生活了数周。

derivatives.zh: terror 加 -ist 后缀，义为「恐怖分子」
terror 加 -ism 后缀，义为「恐怖主义」
同根动词，义为「使惊恐」
同根形容词，义为「可怕的」

senses.title: Intense fear
senses.definition: a very strong feeling of fear
senses.definitionCN: 极为强烈的恐惧感
senses.example: She froze in terror at the sight.
senses.exampleCN: 看到那一幕她吓得僵住了。
senses.why: The Latin root terrere means to frighten, so the noun names the fear itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 terrere 意为「使惊恐」，名词直接命名恐惧本身。

senses.title: Fear used as a weapon
senses.definition: violence meant to frighten people into obedience
senses.definitionCN: 以暴力使人惧服的做法
senses.example: The city lived in terror for weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 全城在恐怖中生活了数周。
senses.why: Fear can be organized and imposed, turning a feeling into a method.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧可以被组织、施加，情绪由此变成手段。

senses.title: A dreadful person or thing
senses.definition: a person or thing that causes great fear or trouble
senses.definitionCN: 引起极大恐惧或麻烦的人或物
senses.example: The new puppy was a little terror in the house.
senses.exampleCN: 新来的小狗把家里搅得鸡飞狗跳。
senses.why: What embodies fear can be named by the fear itself.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧的化身可以径直用恐惧之名指称。

intro.en: Terror comes from Latin terrere, to frighten.
intro.cn: terror 源自拉丁语 terrere（使惊恐）。

items.en: Terrere meant to frighten or scare away.
items.cn: terrere 意为使惊恐、吓退。

items.en: Terror named the resulting fear.
items.cn: terror 指由此产生的恐惧。

items.en: Terreur carried the same sense.
items.cn: 古法语 terreur 义同。

items.en: Terror entered English as intense fear.
items.cn: 14 世纪 terror 进入英语，指强烈恐惧。

items.en: The word also names organized political violence.
items.cn: 现代英语亦指有组织的政治暴力。

note.en: Terror is compared with look-alike words and with words for fear.
note.cn: 把 terror 与形近词及表示恐惧的词作对比。

entries.definition: the general feeling of danger

entries.definition: shock mixed with fear and disgust
entries.definitionCN: 惊骇；混有厌恶

entries.definition: fear of something ahead
entries.definitionCN: 惧怕；侧重对未来的忧虑

abstract.cn: 攥住心脏的一片阴影。

abstract.en: The thing that frightens wears the name of fear.

sensesIntro.en: Terror names the feeling of fear, the method of rule by fear, and what embodies fear.
sensesIntro.cn: terror 命名恐惧之情、恐惧统治之法，以及恐惧的化身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand clutching the heart in the dark.
core.cn: 核心意象：黑暗中攥住心脏的一只手。

branches.en: Pure fear is the root sense.

branches.cn: 被组织的恐惧成为政治暴力。

branches.en: A reign of terror rules by fright.
branches.cn: 恐怖统治靠吓唬维持。

branches.en: The frightening thing borrows the name.
branches.cn: 吓人之物借走了恐惧之名。

branches.en: Terrorism is terror turned system.
branches.cn: 恐怖主义是系统化的恐怖。

latinIntro.en: Terror traces to Latin terrere, to frighten.

definition_zh: 印象；感觉；印记；（书的）印数
definition_en: the idea or feeling you get about someone or something, and also the mark or the number of copies produced by printing
core_image: 刚走进一间陌生会议室时，第一眼看到的样子在脑子里留下的那张快照
scene: 推门进入面试的会议室，椅子的摆法、墙上的钟、说话人的语气，全在一瞬间被记住。 My first impression of the office was that it felt calm and a little old.
sceneCN: 这里 impression 是「印象、感觉」（第 1 个义项：第一眼形成的感觉），句意是我对办公室的第一印象是安静、略带陈旧。画面里有刚推开的会议室门、墙上的钟和那一眼的快照。

pos.zh: 名词：印象、感觉；印记；印数、版次

derivatives.zh: 模仿艺人；印象派画家
印象主义（艺术流派）
易受影响的、易被打动的
印象式的、凭感觉的

senses.title: The feeling you get
senses.definition: the idea or feeling that a person or thing produces in your mind
senses.definitionCN: 人或事物在你心里留下的看法与感觉
senses.example: The city gave me the impression of a place always in a hurry.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市给我的印象是永远在赶时间。
senses.why: The mental sense grew from the physical mark, and it is now the most frequent use of the word.
senses.whyCN: 心理义从物理印痕长出来，如今已是这个词最常见的用法。

senses.title: A mark pressed into a surface
senses.definition: a shape or pattern pressed into wax, clay, or paper
senses.definitionCN: 在蜡、黏土或纸上压出的形状与纹样
senses.example: The ring left an impression in the soft wax.
senses.exampleCN: 戒指在软蜡上留下了一个印子。
senses.why: This is the original sense, still in use when the pressing is literal.
senses.whyCN: 这是最初的义项，当压的动作是真实的，它仍在使用。

senses.title: A printing run
senses.definition: all the copies of a book printed at one time
senses.definitionCN: 一次印刷出来的全部书籍
senses.example: The first impression sold out within a month.
senses.exampleCN: 第一次印刷的版本一个月内就卖完了。
senses.why: Printing presses leave marks on paper, so the word came to name one whole batch of marks.
senses.whyCN: 印刷机在纸上留下印子，于是这个词也用来指同一批印出来的东西。

intro.en: Impression is the noun partner of impress, and it names both the pressing and what the pressing leaves.
intro.cn: impression 是 impress 的名词伙伴，既指「压」这个动作，也指压出来的东西。

items.en: Imprimere meant to press into, and its noun impressio named the act and the mark.
items.cn: 拉丁语 imprimere 意为「压进去」，名词 impressio 既指动作又指印记。

items.en: The root premere, to press, also gave press and pressure, all sharing the same physical image.
items.cn: 词根 premere「压」还给出了 press 与 pressure，共用一个身体性意象。

items.en: Old French carried the noun as impression, still used for seal marks and prints.
items.cn: 古法语以 impression 沿用这个名词，多指印章与压出的图案。

items.en: English took the word in the fourteenth century, and printers soon used it for one run of copies.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入，印刷商不久便用它指一次印刷的数量。

items.en: The modern mental sense took over in the eighteenth century, so that impressions are mostly felt rather than pressed.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，现代的心理义占了上风，如今印象多是感受到的，而不是压出来的。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the impress family; the near-meaning group gathers other words for a mental picture.
note.cn: 形近组收 impress 这一族词；近义组收其他表示「心里图像」的词。

entries.definition: The verb that produces an impression.
entries.definitionCN: 动词形式，产生印象的那一方。

entries.definition: Deserving admiration because of size, skill, or effect.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词「令人印象深刻的」，因规模、技艺或效果而值得赞叹。

entries.definition: A word or look that carries meaning outward.
entries.definitionCN: 「表达、表情」，方向朝外，与前缀相反而对称。

entries.definition: An emotional state, often vaguer than an impression.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「感觉」，比 impression 更模糊、更偏情绪。

entries.definition: The way something is understood through the senses and the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「感知、看法」，强调经由感官与头脑的理解。

entries.definition: A picture held in the mind or presented to others.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「形象、图像」，指心里或对外的画面。

normalIntro.en: The hooks work on the seal image and on the four fixed phrases English builds around the noun.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子围绕印章意象，以及英语中围绕这个名词固定下来的几种搭配。

normal.en: impression is impress with the noun ending -ion, so it is the mark that stays after the pressing.
normal.cn: impression 就是 impress 加名词词尾 -ion，是压完之后留下来的那个印子。

normal.en: Make a good impression is the phrase for first meetings, because the mark set early lasts.
normal.cn: make a good impression 是初次见面专用，因为早压下的印子留得久。

normal.en: Under the impression that means believing something wrongly, as if the mark were mistaken.
normal.cn: under the impression that 表示误以为，好像印子盖错了位置。

normal.en: In printing, the first impression is simply the first run off the press.
normal.cn: 印刷业里，the first impression 就是印机出来的第一版。

normal.en: Impressionism takes its name from a painting whose loose brushwork seemed to be only a first impression.
normal.cn: 印象派得名于一幅画，它松散的笔触看上去只像一次初见的印象。

abstract.en: An impression is a compression of another person into a small mental file.
abstract.cn: 印象就是把另一个人压缩成一份很小的心里档案。

abstract.en: The word reminds us that minds receive as wax receives: early marks are the deepest.
abstract.cn: 这个词提醒我们，心接收的方式像蜡：越早压下的印子越深。

abstract.en: Between what is pressed on us and what we believe was pressed lies most of human misunderstanding.
abstract.cn: 别人压给我们的，和我们以为压过来的之间，横着人类大多数误会。

examples.en: First impressions are hard to change once they form.
examples.cn: 第一印象一旦形成就很难改变。

examples.en: I was under the impression that the shop closed at six.
examples.cn: 我一直以为这家店六点关门。

examples.en: The seal left a clear impression in the red wax.
examples.cn: 印章在红蜡上留下了清晰的印痕。

dict_mnemonic.text: impress 压印 + -ion 名词词尾——压在心上的那道印子，就是印象

root: 拉丁语 impressio「压入、印记」（imprimere 的名词），经古法语 impression 于中世纪英语时期进入英语；先指印章与印版，十八世纪起心理义「印象」成为主用法，印刷业中又指一次印量。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: the feeling someone or something gives you, the physical mark, and one printing run of a book.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：人或事物给你的感觉，物理印痕，以及书籍的一次印量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the mental snapshot taken in the first second of walking into a strange room.
core.cn: 核心意象：推开陌生房间门的头一秒，脑子里拍下的那张快照。

branches.en: THE FEELING: most impressions are now mental rather than physical.
branches.cn: 感觉线：如今多数印象是心理的，而非物理的。

branches.en: THE WAX: the physical mark keeps the oldest sense alive.
branches.cn: 蜡线：物理印痕让最老的义项继续活着。

branches.en: THE PRESS: a printing run is a batch of impressions on paper.
branches.cn: 印机线：一次印量就是纸上的一批印子。

branches.en: THE PHRASE: under the impression means holding a mistaken mark.
branches.cn: 搭配线：under the impression 表示心里盖着一个错的印象。

branches.en: THE FAMILY: impressionable describes a mind like soft wax.
branches.cn: 词族线：impressionable 形容一颗像软蜡一样的心。

intro.en: The table shows -ion nouns beside the verbs and adjectives of the same press family.
intro.cn: 此表把同一 press 家族的 -ion 名词与动词、形容词并排。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is imprimere, from in and premere.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语底子是 imprimere，由 in 与 premere 组成。

items.meaning: a mark or a feeling left behind
items.example: The hall left a strong impression on her.
items.exampleCN: 那座大厅给她留下了强烈的印象。

items.meaning: to press in, to fill with admiration
items.exampleCN: 这个结果让评委们刮目相看。

items.meaningCN: 形容词：令人印象深刻的
items.exampleCN: 她给出了一个令人赞叹的回答。

items.example: Children that age are highly impressionable.
items.exampleCN: 那个年纪的孩子很容易受影响。

items.meaning: the art movement named for a first impression
items.example: Impressionism changed how light was painted.
items.exampleCN: 印象主义改变了画家表现光线的方式。

items.meaning: an artist or performer of impressions
items.meaningCN: 名词：印象派画家；模仿艺人
items.example: The impressionist painted the river at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 那位印象派画家画了黎明的河。

items.meaning: pressing meaning out into words or looks
items.exampleCN: 他的表情没透露任何信息。

items.meaning: a pressing down, of mood or of the land
items.example: The valley is a shallow depression.

latinEntries.meaning: a pressing in, the mark left
latinEntries.meaningCN: 拉丁语名词：压入，留下的印记

definition_zh: 建造者；建筑工人；营造商；开发商；建设者
definition_en: a person or company that builds things, especially houses and other structures
core_image: 戴安全帽的人：把图纸上的线条一块块垒成真实的墙
scene: 工地刚开工，图纸摊在桌上，铁锹和砖块堆在门口，工人们陆续进场。 The builder laid the first row of bricks carefully.
sceneCN: 这里 builder 是「建筑工人；施工者」（第 1 个义项：从事建造的人）；句意是这位建筑工人仔细砌好第一排砖。

pos.zh: 建造者；建筑工人；营造商；开发商

collocations.zh: 现代中国的建设者（比喻用法）

derivatives.zh: 基础词，义为「建造；建立」，builder 由它加施动者后缀 -er 构成
由 build 加名词后缀 -ing 构成，义为「建筑物；建筑」
由 build 加前缀 re- 构成，义为「重建」

senses.title: A person who builds houses or structures
senses.definition: a person whose job is to build houses, walls, and other structures
senses.definitionCN: 以建造房屋、墙壁等结构为职业的人
senses.example: The builder mixed cement before laying the bricks.
senses.exampleCN: 建筑工人砌砖前先搅拌水泥。
senses.why: The agent suffix -er turns the verb build into a person who does it.
senses.whyCN: 施动者后缀 -er 把动词 build 变成「做这件事的人」，最直观的义项就是亲手施工的工人。

senses.title: A company or firm that constructs buildings
senses.definition: a business that constructs buildings, often housing estates or offices
senses.definitionCN: 承接建造业务的商业机构，常指住宅小区或办公楼开发商
senses.example: A local builder is planning a new housing estate on the edge of town.
senses.exampleCN: 一家本地营造商计划在城郊新建住宅区。
senses.why: The agent noun can be applied to organizations, not just individuals.
senses.whyCN: 施动者名词可从个人扩展到机构——「做建造这件事的主体」也可以是一家公司。

senses.title: A person who creates or develops something abstract
senses.definition: someone who develops an institution, a nation, or an idea step by step
senses.definitionCN: 逐步创建机构、国家或理念的人
senses.example: She was remembered as a builder of the modern university.
senses.exampleCN: 她被誉为这所现代大学的缔造者。
senses.why: Construction extends metaphorically from bricks to institutions.
senses.whyCN: 把「垒砖造房」的意象投射到抽象事物上，创建机构就像一砖一瓦地建设。

senses.title: In computing: a tool that assembles products from parts
senses.definition: in computing, a tool or program that assembles a product from components
senses.definitionCN: 计算机领域把组件组装成成品的工具或程序
senses.example: The website builder lets beginners create pages without code.
senses.exampleCN: 这款网站生成器让初学者无需写代码就能创建页面。
senses.why: The metaphor shifts from building physical structures to assembling digital products.
senses.whyCN: 把「组装实体结构」的隐喻搬到软件里，拼装组件生成成品的工具也叫 builder。

senses.title: A body-builder or someone who develops physique
senses.definition: used in compounds for someone who develops muscle or character
senses.definitionCN: 用于复合词，指锻炼肌肉或塑造品格的人
senses.example: He works out daily as an enthusiastic body builder.
senses.exampleCN: 他每天锻炼，是个充满热情的健美者。
senses.why: The image of building extends to shaping one's own body or character.
senses.whyCN: 「建造」的意象进一步延伸到塑造身体或品格，如 body builder（健美者）。

intro.en: Builder is the agent noun of build, formed with the Old English agent suffix -ere.
intro.cn: builder 是动词 build 的施动者名词，由古英语施动者后缀 -ere 构成，词源脉络与 build 一致。

items.en: The root of build is generally traced to a reconstructed form meaning to dwell or to cultivate, though the exact connection is uncertain.
items.cn: build 的词根一般认为可追溯到一个表示「居住；耕作」的重构形式 *bhu-, 具体演变链条存疑。

items.en: The verb build (bilden, byldan) meant to construct a house, and the agent suffix -ere already existed.
items.cn: 古英语动词 bildan 义为「建造房屋」，同时已有施动者后缀 -ere（表示「做某事的人」）。

items.en: The noun builder appears in Middle English around the 14th-15th century, meaning one who constructs.
items.cn: 中古英语时期（约 14 至 15 世纪）出现 builder，义为「建造者」。

items.en: The meaning expanded from individual craftsmen to firms that organize construction work.
items.cn: 近代英语时期，词义从个体工匠扩展到组织施工的商业机构（营造商）。

items.en: The word now covers builders of nations and software, a productive metaphor.
items.cn: 现代英语中 builder 也指国家建设者和软件构建工具，隐喻用法活跃。

note.en: Words that share the build root or look similar, and near concepts in the same field.
note.cn: 本组区分与 build 同根的词、拼写相近的词，以及建筑领域内的近义概念。

entries.definition: a structure with walls and a roof
entries.definitionCN: 建筑物；楼房；也指建筑行业（与 builder 同根，均为 build 的派生词）

entries.definition: a shop selling materials for construction
entries.definitionCN: 建材供应商（含 builder 的复合词，属同一词族）

entries.definition: a large rounded rock
entries.definitionCN: 巨砾；大圆石（只是拼写相近，词源与 build 无关）

entries.definition: a person or company that constructs things
entries.definitionCN: 建造者；施工方（较正式，多用于工程语境）

entries.definition: a firm hired to carry out building work

entries.definition: a person who designs buildings

definition_zh: 向……保证；使确信；确保
definition_en: to tell someone confidently that something is true, or to make it certain
core_image: 一只手按住对方的手背，说一句放心
scene: 登机前机长在广播里说明情况。 The captain assured us that the flight was safe.
sceneCN: 这里 assure 是「向……保证」（第 1 个义项：让对方确信某事）；句意是机长向我们保证航班安全。

pos.zh: 动词：向……保证；使确信；确保

derivatives.zh: 名词：保证；信心
形容词：确信的；有把握的
形容词：令人安心的

senses.title: Make someone certain
senses.definition: to tell someone confidently that something is true so they stop worrying
senses.definitionCN: 肯定地告诉对方某事为真，使其不再担心
senses.example: The captain assured us that the flight was safe.
senses.exampleCN: 机长向我们保证航班是安全的。
senses.why: Assure comes from Latin assecurare, 'to make secure', built on securus 'free from care', so the core act is removing someone's worry rather than merely stating a fact.
senses.whyCN: assure 源自拉丁语 assecurare「使安全」，词基 securus 意为「无忧」，所以它的核心是替对方消除担心，而不只是陈述事实。

senses.title: Make certain to happen
senses.definition: to make something certain to happen or be obtained
senses.definitionCN: 使某事确定发生或确定得到
senses.example: Hard work assured his place in the team.
senses.exampleCN: 努力让他在队里站稳了位置。
senses.why: When the calming is done by events rather than words, the same 'make secure' means making an outcome certain.
senses.whyCN: 当让人安心的不是言语而是事情本身时，同一个「使稳固」就变成让某个结果确定无疑。

intro.en: Assure began as a word about making people free from care.
intro.cn: assure 起初是个让人免于忧虑的词。

items.en: securus meant 'free from care'.
items.cn: securus 意为「无忧的」。

items.en: assecurare meant 'to make secure'.
items.cn: assecurare 意为「使安稳」。

items.en: asseurer meant 'to promise and calm'.
items.cn: asseurer 意为「保证并安抚」。

items.en: English assure covered both promising and securing.
items.cn: 英语 assure 兼指保证与确保。

items.en: The word settled in formal promises and insurance.
items.cn: 这个词固定在正式承诺与保险语境中。

note.en: The look-alike group is the sure family; the near-meaning group gives verbs of promising.
note.cn: 形近组是 sure 词族；近义组是表示承诺的动词。

entries.definition: a promise or confidence

entries.definitionCN: 使安心

entries.definitionCN: 承诺

entries.definitionCN: 使信服

normalIntro.en: To assure is to hand someone a reason to stop worrying.
normalIntro.cn: assure 就是递给对方一个不必担心的理由。

normal.en: The object is a person: assure the passengers.
normal.cn: 宾语是人：向乘客保证。

normal.en: Use assure someone of something or assure someone that.

normal.cn: rest assured 是固定说法，意为请放心。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with ensure, which means make certain.
normal.cn: 不要与 ensure 混淆，后者意为确保。

normal.en: The ending sounds like sure.
normal.cn: 词尾读音与 sure 相同。

abstract.en: See a hand pressed briefly over another hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在另一只手背上轻按一下。

abstract.en: See a seat belt sign switched off after the words are spoken.
abstract.cn: 想象广播说完后安全带指示灯熄灭。

abstract.en: See a knot pulled tight so it cannot slip.
abstract.cn: 想象一个结被拉紧，不会松开。

examples.en: The captain assured us that the flight was safe.
examples.cn: 机长向我们保证航班是安全的。

examples.en: Hard work assured his place in the team.
examples.cn: 努力让他在队里站稳了位置。

examples.en: She assured me of her support.
examples.cn: 她向我保证会支持我。

dict_mnemonic.text: as-（向）加 sure（安稳）：把安稳送到对方心里，就是让对方确信；把事情办到没有疑问，就是确保。

root: 源自拉丁语 assecurare「使安稳」，词基 securus 意为「无忧」，经古法语 asseurer 进入英语；由「让人安心」引申为口头保证，再由「使确定」引申为确保。

sensesIntro.en: Words can calm a person, and facts can settle an outcome; both remove doubt.
sensesIntro.cn: 言语能安抚人，事实能定下结果，两者都在消除疑问。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pressed down to steady another.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手按下去，让另一只手稳住。

branches.cn: 安抚乘客

latinIntro.en: Latin securus, 'free from care', also gives secure and security.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 securus「无忧」也是 secure 与 security 的来源。

definition_zh: 特征；特色；面容的一部分；以…为特色
definition_en: a distinctive quality, an important part of a product, a part of the face, or to include something as a main part
core_image: 手机展开成一块大屏，发布会的大屏幕上正循环播放这个动作
scene: 这款手机最大的卖点是能折起来放进口袋。 A folding screen is the phone's best feature.
sceneCN: 这里 feature 是「特色；卖点」（第 2 个义项）；句意：折叠屏是这款手机最大的特色。

senses.title: A distinctive quality
senses.definition: a quality that makes something recognizably different
senses.definitionCN: 使某物可辨认地与众不同的性质
senses.example: Patience is a feature of good teachers.
senses.exampleCN: 耐心是好老师的一个特点。
senses.why: This is the broad sense of a notable quality.
senses.whyCN: 这是表示显著性质的宽泛义。

senses.title: An important product part
senses.definition: an important or attractive part of a product or service
senses.definitionCN: 产品或服务中重要或有吸引力之处
senses.example: The camera is the phone's best feature.
senses.exampleCN: 相机是这款手机最大的特色。
senses.why: Companies highlight features that make a product special.
senses.whyCN: 公司会突出让产品与众不同的卖点。

senses.title: A part of the face
senses.definition: one of the parts that make up a person's face
senses.definitionCN: 构成人脸的一个部分
senses.example: Her features were calm and serious.
senses.exampleCN: 她的面容平静而严肃。
senses.why: The shape sense narrowed to parts of the face.
senses.whyCN: 「形状」义缩小为面部的各部分。

senses.title: To include prominently
senses.definition: to include something or someone as an important part
senses.definitionCN: 把某事物或某人作为重要部分纳入
senses.example: The film features a young violinist.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影由一位年轻小提琴手主演。
senses.why: The noun turns into a verb of putting forward.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为表示突出展示的动词。

intro.en: Feature comes from Latin factura, a making or form, through Old French faiture.
intro.cn: feature 经古法语 faiture 源自拉丁语 factura（制作、形态）。

items.en: Factura meant a making or the form produced.
items.cn: factura 意为制作或制作出的形态。

items.cn: faiture 表示形状与外貌。

items.en: Feature first meant shape or form.
items.cn: feature 最初表示形状或外形。

items.en: The word narrowed to parts of the face.
items.cn: 该词缩小为面部的各部分。

items.en: Feature widened again to notable parts and product qualities.
items.cn: 现代英语中该词又扩展为显著部分与产品特色。

note.en: Feature is compared with similar-looking words and with words for qualities.

sceneCN: 这里是「痛苦、苦难」（第 1 个义项：长期的痛苦处境）；句意为在援助到来之前，多年的苦难已经把这一家人拖垮了。图中可辨识物件：没有生火的屋子、敲窗的雨、拉到下巴的旧毯子。

senses.title: Great unhappiness or suffering
senses.definition: a state of deep unhappiness and pain, especially one that lasts over a long period
senses.definitionCN: 深深的痛苦与难受，尤指持续很久的状态
senses.example: Years of misery had worn the family down before help arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 在援助到来之前，多年的苦难已经把这一家人拖垮了。
senses.why: Latin miseria named wretchedness as a condition, so misery begins as a place a person is stuck in rather than as a mood that passes through.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 miseria 把悲惨说成一种处境，所以 misery 起初是一个人被困住的地方，而不是一阵会过去的心情。

senses.title: A cause or source of hardship
senses.definition: something such as poverty, illness or loss that brings suffering to people
senses.definitionCN: 贫穷、疾病或丧失之类给人带来痛苦的事
senses.example: The flood brought misery to hundreds of villages.
senses.exampleCN: 那场洪水给数百个村庄带来了苦难。
senses.why: Once miseria names the condition, the things that produce it can take the same word, because English often lets a cause borrow the name of its effect.
senses.whyCN: miseria 一旦指这种处境，制造这种处境的事物也能用同一个词，因为英语常让原因借用结果的名字。

senses.title: A person who complains all the time
senses.definition: in informal British use, someone who is habitually gloomy and complains about everything
senses.definitionCN: 英国口语用法，指一贯阴郁、对什么都抱怨的人
senses.example: Don't be such a misery and come to the party.
senses.exampleCN: 别这么爱抱怨了，来参加聚会吧。
senses.why: The word moves from the feeling to the person who carries it into a room; a misery is someone whose company spreads the very state the noun names.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从感受转到把感受带进房间的人；一个 misery 就是那种一在场就把这种状态扩散开来的人。

intro.en: Misery comes from Latin miseria, the noun for wretchedness built on miser, and it reached English by way of Old French.
intro.cn: misery 来自拉丁语 miseria，即建立在 miser 之上、表示悲惨处境的名称，经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Miseria named wretchedness, hardship and distress, and it was formed directly on miser, the word for a wretched person.
items.cn: miseria 意为悲惨、困苦、痛苦，直接由表示可怜人的 miser 构成。

items.en: Miser described someone unhappy, pitiable or living in bad circumstances, and it supplied the root for the whole family.
items.cn: miser 形容一个人不快乐、可怜或境遇糟糕，为整个词族提供了词根。

items.en: Old French took miseria as misere, meaning distress and hardship, and passed it on to English.
items.cn: 古法语把 miseria 写作 misere，意为痛苦与困苦，并把它传给英语。

items.en: Middle English misery covered both the state of suffering and the events that caused it.
items.cn: 中古英语的 misery 既指受苦的状态，也指造成痛苦的事件。

items.en: Modern English kept the serious sense and added an informal one for a person who complains without end.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了严肃的义项，又增加了一个口语义，指没完没了抱怨的人。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the same Latin miser and two neighbours that only share its shape; the near-meaning group collects words for suffering and for deep sorrow.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在同一个拉丁词 miser 上的词，以及两个只在字形上相近的词；近义组收表示受苦与深切悲伤的词。

entries.definition: Very severe mental or physical pain.

normalIntro.en: The word rests on a Latin noun for wretchedness; its family keeps returning to the state of suffering, the events that cause it, and the people who carry it into a room.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在表示悲惨处境的拉丁语名词上，同族词反复回到受苦的状态、造成痛苦的事件，以及把痛苦带进房间的人。

normal.en: Miseria is Latin for wretchedness, and it was built on miser, the word for a wretched person.
normal.cn: miseria 是拉丁语中表示悲惨的词，建立在表示可怜人的 miser 上。

normal.en: Misery keeps the same root as miserable, but the noun names the state while the adjective names the person or thing inside it.
normal.cn: misery 与 miserable 同根，但名词指状态，形容词指处在状态里的人或物。

normal.en: The plural miseries names specific hardships, because a long state of suffering is usually made of many separate blows.
normal.cn: 复数 miseries 指一桩桩具体的不幸，因为长期的受苦通常由许多次打击组成。

normal.en: The phrase 「put someone out of their misery」 first meant to end a creature's suffering, and it now also means to end someone's suspense.
normal.cn: 「put someone out of their misery」起初指结束一个生灵的痛苦，现在也指让某人不必再猜。

normal.en: 「Misery loves company」 is an old saying that treats sorrow as something looking for other people to sit beside.
normal.cn: 「misery loves company」是一句老话，把悲伤看成会去找别人来陪坐的东西。

abstract.en: A cold room with a dying lamp is misery as a place a person cannot leave, not as a mood that passes.
abstract.cn: 一间冷屋子加上一盏将灭的灯，就是 misery：它是人离不开的地方，而不是会过去的心情。

abstract.en: Because the noun names both the feeling and its causes, a flood, a debt and a long illness can all be called miseries.
abstract.cn: 因为这个名词既指感受也指成因，一场洪水、一笔债和一场久病都能叫 miseries。

abstract.en: Calling a complainer a misery suggests that sorrow can spread from one person into a whole room.
abstract.cn: 把一个抱怨者叫作 misery，说明悲伤能从一个人扩散到整个房间。

examples.en: Years of misery had worn the family down before help arrived.
examples.cn: 在援助到来之前，多年的苦难已经把这一家人拖垮了。

examples.en: The flood brought misery to hundreds of villages.
examples.cn: 那场洪水给数百个村庄带来了苦难。

examples.en: Don't be such a misery and come to the party.
examples.cn: 别这么爱抱怨了，来参加聚会吧。
