senses.title: Including everything
senses.definition: covering or including all parts, without leaving anything out
senses.definitionCN: 涵盖或包括所有部分，不遗漏任何一项
senses.example: The overall cost of the project was higher than planned.
senses.exampleCN: 项目的总成本高于计划。
senses.why: Overall began as over + all, 'everywhere, in every part'. The modern 1894 sense 'taking all into consideration' keeps the same picture: the word spreads over the whole instead of standing inside one part.
senses.whyCN: overall 原为 over + all，意为“到处、在每个部分”。1894 年的现代义“把一切考虑在内”保留同一画面：这个词铺在整个整体之上，而不是站在某一部分里。

senses.title: The total amount
senses.definition: the combined amount after all parts have been added together
senses.definitionCN: 把所有部分相加后的合计量
senses.example: Overall spending rose by six percent.
senses.exampleCN: 总支出上升了百分之六。
senses.why: Once the word covers all parts, it can name their sum. The movement is from spatial coverage to arithmetic total: everything is gathered under one figure.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词覆盖所有部分，它就能命名它们的总和。意义从空间覆盖转到算术合计：一切被收拢到一个数字之下。

senses.title: A general impression
senses.definition: a judgment based on the whole rather than on separate details
senses.definitionCN: 基于整体而非各个细节作出的判断
senses.example: My overall impression was of a well-run school.
senses.exampleCN: 我的总体印象是这是一所管理良好的学校。
senses.why: An impression formed 'over all' is built by stepping back from details. The word marks the level at which separate observations merge into one feeling.
senses.whyCN: “覆盖全部”形成的印象，是从细节退后一步得到的。这个词标记的是各个观察合并成一种感受的那个层级。

senses.title: The whole picture
senses.definition: the complete situation seen as one connected picture
senses.definitionCN: 作为一个相互关联的整体来看的完整局面
senses.example: The report gives an overall picture of the region.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告给出了该地区的整体图景。
senses.why: The metaphor is visual: an observer moves above the parts and sees how they fit. Overall names that altitude of view, not the individual objects below.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻是视觉性的：观察者升到各部分之上，看见它们如何拼合。overall 命名的是这个观察高度，而不是下方的单个物体。

senses.title: Generally speaking
senses.definition: used to sum up a judgment after weighing the details
senses.definitionCN: 在权衡细节之后用来概括判断
senses.example: Overall, the experiment succeeded.
senses.exampleCN: 总体来说，实验是成功的。
senses.why: As an adverb, the word performs the summing-up act itself. It tells the listener that the sentence to follow is a verdict after the parts have been counted, not another detail.
senses.whyCN: 作副词时，这个词本身就在做“汇总”这个动作。它告诉听者：接下来的句子是清点完各部分后的裁决，而不是又一条细节。

senses.title: Overalls: a garment worn over all
senses.titleCN: 工装裤：穿在其他衣服外面的衣物
senses.definition: a protective garment, usually trousers with a bib, worn over ordinary clothes
senses.definitionCN: 穿在日常衣服外面的防护衣物，通常是有胸兜的裤子
senses.example: The mechanic wiped his hands on his overalls.
senses.exampleCN: 机修工在工装裤上擦了擦手。
senses.why: The noun overalls uses the literal spatial sense: a garment worn over all the other clothes. The same 'covering everything' idea that governs the adjective is here made of cloth.
senses.whyCN: 名词 overalls 用的是字面空间义：穿在所有其他衣服外面的衣物。支配形容词的“覆盖全部”观念，在这里是用布做成的。

senses.title: Combined-score champion
senses.definition: the winner judged on the total of all events rather than a single one
senses.definitionCN: 按所有项目的总和而非单项评出的优胜者
senses.example: She took the overall title by two points.
senses.exampleCN: 她以两分之差拿下总冠军。
senses.why: In sport, overall marks the level at which separate events are added into one standing. The word directs attention away from any single race and toward the whole series.
senses.whyCN: 在体育中，overall 标记的是把各单项加总成一个总排名的层级。这个词把注意力从任何一场比赛移开，转向整个系列赛。

senses.title: Whole-system responsibility
senses.definition: responsibility for the whole of an operation rather than one part of it
senses.definitionCN: 对整个运作而非某一部分负责
senses.example: He has overall responsibility for safety.
senses.exampleCN: 他对安全负总责。
senses.why: This use turns the spatial word into an organizational one: a person stands above all the parts and answers for how they work together. Coverage becomes accountability.
senses.whyCN: 这一用法把空间词变成组织词：一个人站在所有部分之上，对它们如何协同负责。覆盖变成了问责。

intro.en: Overall is native English, built from over and all. Its oldest sense was 'everywhere'; the modern 'all things considered' is only from 1894.
intro.cn: overall 是英语本族词，由 over 与 all 构成。最古老的义项是“到处”；现代“把所有事都考虑在内”的义项直到 1894 年才出现。

items.en: The phrase ofer eall meant 'everywhere, in every part or place'. The modern spelling overall comes from Middle English over-al.
items.cn: 短语 ofer eall 意为“到处、在每个部分或地方”。现代拼写 overall 来自中世纪英语 over-al。

items.en: Over-al kept the sense 'everywhere'. That original sense is now obsolete in standard English.
items.cn: over-al 保留“到处”之义。这个原始义项在现代标准英语中已废弃。

items.en: The modern meaning 'including everything, taking all into consideration' is recorded.
items.cn: 现代义“包括一切、把全部考虑在内”被记录。

items.en: The garment sense of overalls (trousers worn over other clothes) belongs to the same literal idea of something worn over all.
items.cn: overalls（穿在其他衣服外面的裤子）的衣物义，同属“穿在所有东西外面”这一字面观念。具体年代各家说法不一，此处只取通行理解。

items.en: The word now works as adjective, adverb, and noun. Its unity is the idea of a view or covering that spans every part.
items.cn: 这个词现在是形容词、副词和名词。它的统一性在于一个横跨每个部分的视角或覆盖。

note.en: The look-alike group separates other over- compounds; the near-meaning group ranks words by how much they include.
note.cn: 形近组区分其他 over- 复合词；近义组按“包含多少”来区分。

entries.definition: too much; excessively. It is over- with the negative sense 'too', not 'covering all'.
entries.definitionCN: 过度地；太。它用的是 over- 的负面义“太”，不是“覆盖全部”。

entries.definition: above one's head; also fixed business costs. The over- is spatial or figurative, not inclusive.
entries.definitionCN: 头顶上的；也指企业固定开销。这里的 over- 是空间或比喻义，不表示“包括”。

entries.definition: beyond the sea. The over- means 'across', not 'covering everything'.
entries.definitionCN: 海外的。over- 表示“越过”，不是“覆盖一切”。

entries.definition: complete in amount; the whole sum. It is quantitative, while overall can also mean a general judgment.
entries.definitionCN: 数量上完整的；总和。它偏数量，而 overall 也可指总体判断。

entries.definition: covering the main features rather than details. It stresses breadth of scope, not the act of summing up.
entries.definitionCN: 涵盖主要特征而非细节。它强调范围的宽，而不是汇总的动作。

entries.definition: including nearly all relevant items. It is stronger and more formal than overall and usually implies a deliberate completeness.
entries.definitionCN: 包括几乎所有相关项目。它比 overall 更强、更正式，通常暗示刻意的完整。

entries.definition: considering everything; generally. It is the adverbial phrase closest to overall in its summing-up use.
entries.definitionCN: 总的来说；大体上。它是最接近 overall 汇总用法的副词短语。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks on over + all, then three abstract images of a view from above.
normalIntro.cn: 先给五个 over + all 的钩子，再用三个“从高处看”的抽象画面。

normal.en: over + all: the view that goes over every part.
normal.cn: over + all：越过每一个部分的视角。

normal.en: overall ends with all, so it always includes everything.
normal.cn: overall 以 all 结尾，所以它总是把一切包含进来。

normal.en: overalls are worn over all your other clothes: same word, made of cloth.
normal.cn: overalls 穿在你所有其他衣服外面：同一个词，只是用布做成了。

normal.en: Overall, the plan works: the comma marks the step back from details.
normal.cn: Overall, the plan works：这个逗号标记从细节退后一步。

normal.en: An overall winner is not the winner of one race but of the whole series.
normal.cn: overall winner 不是某一场比赛的赢家，而是整个系列赛的赢家。

abstract.en: To see overall is to change altitude: details do not disappear, they become pattern.
abstract.cn: 看“整体”就是换高度：细节没有消失，而是变成了图案。

abstract.en: Every whole is a decision about which parts to count and which to leave outside the frame.
abstract.cn: 每个“整体”都是一次决定：哪些部分算进来，哪些留在画框之外。

abstract.en: Overall judgment is what remains after the numbers stop arguing with each other.
abstract.cn: 总体判断，就是数字之间不再互相争吵之后剩下的东西。

examples.en: Overall, the trip was a success despite the delays.
examples.cn: 尽管有延误，总体来说这次旅行是成功的。

examples.en: The overall budget includes travel, staff, and equipment.
examples.cn: 总预算包括差旅、人员与设备。

examples.en: He wore overalls and a heavy shirt in the workshop.
examples.cn: 他在车间里穿着工装裤和厚衬衫。

sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从空间覆盖，走到总量、印象、整体图景、汇总副词、衣物、综合头衔与整体责任。

branches.cn: 感知：退后一步形成的印象或图景。

branches.en: The adverb as a verdict: the sentence that follows is a summary.
branches.cn: 副词作裁决：接下来的句子是一个总结。

branches.en: Clothing: the literal covering worn over all other clothes.
branches.cn: 衣物：字面意义上穿在所有其他衣服外面的覆盖物。

branches.en: Institutions: a combined title, or accountability for the whole.
branches.cn: 制度层面：综合头衔，或对整个体系负责。

intro.en: Overall is a transparent compound of two very old native words. The over- prefix is shared with a large family; the all half is equally productive.
intro.cn: overall 是两个非常古老的英语本族词构成的透明复合词。over- 前缀与一个庞大词族共享，all 这一半也同样能产。

latinIntro.en: No Latin entry applies: over is Old English ofer (PIE *uper), and all is Old English eall, of uncertain connections outside Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 不适用拉丁词条：over 是古英语 ofer（原始印欧语 *uper），all 是古英语 eall，其在日耳曼语之外的关联不确定。

items.meaning: covering everything; considered as a whole
items.meaningCN: 覆盖一切；作为整体来考虑

items.meaning: a garment worn over other clothes
items.meaningCN: 穿在其他衣服外面的工装
items.example: The painter put on his overalls.
The plane flew over the city.

items.meaning: a majority of all votes cast, not just of one group
items.meaningCN: 全部票数中的绝对多数
items.example: The party won an overall majority.
The project has one overarching goal.
items.exampleCN: 这个项目有一个总揽全局的目标。

definition_zh: 依赖；依靠；信任
definition_en: to depend on someone or something for support, help, or truth
core_image: 把自己整个人倚靠在一根结实的柱子上
scene: 停电的夜里，整条街只有这家小店的灯还亮着，邻居们都来买蜡烛。 When the power failed, the whole street relied on the little shop that still had candles.
sceneCN: 这里 rely 是「依靠」（第 1 个义项：需要某人或某物提供支持）；句意：停电之后，整条街都依靠那家还有蜡烛的小店。

collocations.phrase: rely on sb to do sth

derivatives.zh: rely 加 -able 构成，义为「可靠的」
rely 加 -ance 构成，义为「依赖；依靠」
reliable 加 -ly 构成，义为「可靠地」

senses.title: To depend on for support
senses.definition: to need someone or something in order to live, work, or succeed
senses.definitionCN: 为生活、工作或成功而需要某人或某物
senses.example: The village relies on the river for drinking water.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村庄依靠这条河获取饮用水。
senses.why: The Latin source means to bind fast, so the core image is leaning your whole weight on something tied in place.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词源意为「牢牢系住」，所以核心画面是把整个人的重量倚在系牢的东西上。

senses.title: To trust someone to be dependable
senses.definition: to believe that someone will do what they promised or that something is true
senses.definitionCN: 相信某人会履行承诺，或相信某事是真的
senses.example: You can rely on her to keep a secret.
senses.exampleCN: 你可以相信她会保守秘密。
senses.why: Leaning on a tied post requires believing it will not move, and that confidence becomes the sense of trust.
senses.whyCN: 倚靠一根系牢的柱子，前提是相信它不会移动，这份信心就发展为「信任」。

intro.en: Rely comes from Old French relier, to bind together, which descends from Latin religare.
intro.cn: rely 来自古法语 relier「绑在一起」，可追溯到拉丁语 religare。

items.en: Religare joins re- with ligare, to bind, and means to tie something fast.
items.cn: religare 由 re- 与 ligare「捆绑」组合，意为牢牢系住。

items.en: The same verb is one of the proposed sources of the noun religion.
items.cn: 这个动词也是名词 religion 的候选词源之一。

items.en: Relier means to bind together, to attach, and to fasten.
items.cn: 古法语 relier 表示绑在一起、连接、系紧。

items.en: English rely first means to attach oneself to a person or a party.
items.cn: 英语中的 rely 最初表示把自己依附于某个人或某个团体。

items.en: From attachment comes dependence, and from dependence comes the everyday sense of trusting.
items.cn: 从依附生出依靠，再从依靠生出日常所说的信任。

note.en: Rely is a binding word at heart, and its family includes reliable and reliance.
note.cn: rely 本质上是一个「系住」的词，词族包括 reliable 与 reliance。

entries.definition: able to be trusted to do what is expected
entries.definitionCN: 可靠的；可信赖的，由 rely 加 -able 构成

entries.definition: the state of depending on someone or something
entries.definitionCN: 依赖；依靠，由 rely 加 -ance 构成

entries.definition: a system of faith and worship
entries.definitionCN: 宗教，与 rely 共享拉丁语 religare 词源

entries.definition: to need someone or something in order to survive or succeed
entries.definitionCN: 依靠；取决于，是最常见的近义词

entries.definition: to believe that someone is honest and will not harm you
entries.definitionCN: 信任，侧重对人的信心

entries.definition: to depend on someone to do what you expect
entries.definitionCN: 指望；依靠，口语中很常用

normalIntro.en: Rely descends from a verb meaning to bind, so the hooks lean on ropes, knots, and steady posts.
normalIntro.cn: rely 源自表示「捆绑」的动词，所以记忆钩子围绕绳索、结和稳固的柱子。

normal.en: The same Latin verb religare also stands behind religion, both about being tied.
normal.cn: 同一个拉丁动词 religare 也是 religion 的来源，两者都关乎「被系住」。

normal.en: Add -able for reliable and -ance for reliance, keeping the y as i before the endings.
normal.cn: 加 -able 得 reliable，加 -ance 得 reliance，加词尾前把 y 变成 i。

normal.en: The past tense relied and the adjective reliable share the same changed spelling.
normal.cn: 过去式 relied 与形容词 reliable 共享同样的拼写变化。

normal.en: The verb always takes on or upon, never a direct object.
normal.cn: 这个动词总是接 on 或 upon，不能直接带宾语。

normal.en: Rely heavily on is the natural phrase for talking about technology and oil.
normal.cn: 谈技术和石油时，rely heavily on 是最自然的说法。

abstract.en: Picture a climber clipping the rope to a steel ring before leaning back.
abstract.cn: 想象攀岩者在后仰之前把绳子扣进钢环。

abstract.en: See a house leaning against an old stone wall in a storm.
abstract.cn: 想象暴风雨中一座房子倚着古老的石墙。

abstract.en: Think of a child holding one finger of an adult in a crowd.
abstract.cn: 想象拥挤人群里，孩子只抓住大人的一根手指。

examples.en: Many small farms rely on rain rather than irrigation.
examples.cn: 许多小农场靠降雨而不是灌溉。

examples.en: We can rely on him to finish the job on time.
examples.cn: 我们可以指望他按时完成工作。

examples.en: The company relies heavily on overseas sales.
examples.cn: 这家公司严重依赖海外销售。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞来」——瑞气来了，可以放心靠上去；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 relier（绑在一起），源自拉丁语 religare（re-「牢牢地」+ ligare「捆绑」）。

sensesIntro.en: One image of leaning on something tied down gives two senses: needing it for support and trusting it to hold.
sensesIntro.cn: 「倚靠系牢之物」这一个画面生出两个义项：需要它提供支撑，以及相信它撑得住。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: leaning your whole weight on a firmly tied post.
core.cn: 核心意象：把整个人的重量倚在系牢的柱子上。

branches.en: The tied post becomes the thing you cannot do without.
branches.cn: 系牢的柱子变成了离不开的依靠。

branches.en: The same post is trusted not to shift, which is the sense of trust.
branches.cn: 同一根柱子被相信不会移动，这就是信任义。

branches.en: Need and trust are two sides of the same leaning.
branches.cn: 需要与信任是同一个倚靠动作的两面。

branches.en: Trust in a person grows from trusting the post to hold.
branches.cn: 对人的信任，是从相信柱子撑得住那里长出来的。

branches.en: Dependence is the plain fact of needing support.
branches.cn: 依赖就是需要支撑这个朴素事实。

intro.en: Rely is a short French borrowing whose Latin parts are still visible in related words.
intro.cn: rely 是一个简短的法语借词，其拉丁成分在相关词中仍清晰可见。

latinIntro.en: Latin re- means back or firmly, and ligare means to bind, so the pair means to bind fast.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁前缀 re- 表示「回、牢牢地」，ligare 表示「捆绑」，两者合起来就是牢牢系住。

items.example: Re- strengthens the binding in religare.
items.exampleCN: 在 religare 中，前缀 re- 强化了捆绑的动作。

items.example: The lig- root returns in ligament and obligation.
items.exampleCN: lig- 词根也出现在 ligament 与 obligation 中。

items.example: Ligare is the source of the lig- root.
items.exampleCN: ligare 是 lig- 词根的来源。

items.example: Reliable means able to be relied on.
items.exampleCN: reliable 意为「可以被依靠的」。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或行为的名词词尾
items.example: Reliance names the state of depending on something.
Relier is the form English rely comes from.
items.exampleCN: relier 是英语 rely 所来自的形式。

items.example: Religare links rely to religion in form.
items.exampleCN: religare 在形式上把 rely 与 religion 联系起来。

items.example: Ligament shows the lig- root in the body.
items.exampleCN: ligament 展示了 lig- 词根在身体上的应用。

derivatives.zh: 可靠的；可信赖的
依赖；依靠
可靠地

definition_zh: 否则；不然；在其他方面；除此之外；以别的方式
definition_en: in a different way, in other respects, or as the other result that follows if something does not happen
core_image: 一条路在岔口分成两支，一块木牌倒在左边，指向右边的那条路几乎没人走过
scene: 末班车的时间已经过了，站台上只剩一个人，他看了看表，又看了看暗下来的街口。 You should leave now, otherwise you will miss the last train.
sceneCN: 这里的 otherwise 是「否则、不然」（第 1 个义项：如果不这样，就会有另一种结果）；句意为你现在就该走，否则会错过末班车。图中可辨识物件：站台、手表、暗下的街口。

pos.zh: 否则；不然；在其他方面；以别的方式

derivatives.zh: otherwise 的前半部分，来自古英语形容词 other，义为「另一个；别的」
由 other 加 -ness 构成，义为「他者性；异质性」
由 other 与 world 复合，再加 -ly 构成，义为「超凡脱俗的」

senses.title: If not this, then something else will happen
senses.definition: used to say what will happen if the action just mentioned is not taken
senses.definitionCN: 用来指出若不做刚提到的那件事，就会出现另一种结果
senses.example: You should leave now, otherwise you will miss the last train.
senses.exampleCN: 你现在就该走，否则会错过末班车。
senses.why: The word began as an Old English phrase meaning in other ways, so the second clause describes the other way things can go.
senses.whyCN: 这个词起初是一句古英语短语，意为「以别的方式」，所以后一个分句说的就是事情可能走的另一种方式。

senses.title: In other respects, apart from what was just said
senses.definition: used to add that something is true apart from the one point already mentioned
senses.definitionCN: 用来补充说明，除了刚才提到的那一点之外，其他方面是成立的
senses.example: The room is small but otherwise comfortable.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间虽小，其他方面却舒适。
senses.why: If the phrase means in other ways, it can also mean with regard to other matters, and that is how it moves from a condition to an exception.
senses.whyCN: 既然这句话意为「以别的方式」，它也就能指「就其他事情而言」，于是从假设的条件转成了例外的补充。

senses.title: In a different way, not like that
senses.definition: in another manner, especially when the manner just thought of was not possible
senses.definitionCN: 以另一种方式，尤指刚想到的那种方式并不可行时
senses.example: There was no choice; he could not have acted otherwise.
senses.exampleCN: 当时别无选择，他不可能有别的做法。
senses.why: The oldest sense survives intact here: otherwise simply says by another way, without implying any condition or exception.
senses.whyCN: 最老的意思在这里完好地保留下来：otherwise 只说明「用另一种方式」，既不表条件，也不表例外。

intro.en: Otherwise is a frozen Old English phrase, on other wise, meaning in other ways; the two words fused into one adverb, and English later also used it as a conjunction.
intro.cn: otherwise 是一句凝固下来的古英语短语，原文意为「以别的方式」；两个词合成一个副词，英语后来又把它用作连词。

items.en: Other came from Old English oþer, meaning the second of two or simply a different one.
items.cn: other 来自古英语 oþer，意为两者中的另一个，或只是「不同的那一个」。

items.en: Wise was an old noun for manner or way, unrelated to the adjective meaning clever, and it survives in words such as likewise.
items.cn: wise 是表示方式、样子的古老名词，与表示「聪明」的形容词无关，它还活在 likewise 这类词里。

items.en: The phrase on oþre wisan meant in other ways, and it was used to describe an alternative course of action.
items.cn: 短语 on oþre wisan 意为「以别的方式」，用来描述另一种做法。

items.en: Middle English wrote the phrase as a single word, otherwise, and widened it to mean in other respects as well.
items.cn: 中古英语把这句短语写成一个词 otherwise，并把意思扩展到「在其他方面」。

items.en: Modern English uses otherwise as an adverb and a conjunction, with fixed phrases such as or otherwise and otherwise known as.
items.cn: 现代英语让 otherwise 兼作副词与连词，并有 or otherwise、otherwise known as 等固定说法。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on other and its family; the near-meaning group collects ways of naming an alternative.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在 other 及其词族的词；近义组收表示「另一种选择」的说法。

entries.definition: A different person or thing, or the second of two.
entries.definitionCN: 不同的人或物，或两者中的另一个。

entries.definition: One more, or a different one.
entries.definitionCN: 再一个，或另一个不同的。

entries.definition: The state of being different from what is familiar.
entries.definitionCN: 与熟悉之物不同的状态。

entries.definition: More concerned with a spiritual world than with daily life.
entries.definitionCN: 更关注精神世界而非日常生活的。

entries.definition: Other than what has been mentioned, or in addition.
entries.definitionCN: 除已提到的之外，或另外。

entries.definition: As another possible choice or option.
entries.definitionCN: 作为另一种可能的选择。

entries.definition: A phrase warning of a bad result if something is not done.
entries.definitionCN: 警告若不照做就会有坏结果的短语。

normalIntro.en: Otherwise is a whole Old English phrase squeezed into one word, so its hooks keep the picture of a second way of doing something.
normalIntro.cn: otherwise 是一整句古英语短语被压成一个词，所以记忆钩子保留「做同一件事的第二种方式」的画面。

normal.en: The word is on other wise in Old English, literally in other ways, and the modern spelling simply fuses the pieces.
normal.cn: 这个词在古英语里写作 on other wise，字面就是「以别的方式」，现代拼写只是把几块合在了一起。

normal.en: Wise here is an old noun for manner, not the adjective for clever, which is why otherwise has nothing to do with being smart.
normal.cn: 这里的 wise 是表示方式的古老名词，而不是表示「聪明」的形容词，所以 otherwise 与聪明无关。

normal.en: The same -wise family gives likewise and clockwise, both of which name a way of doing or going.
normal.cn: 同一个 -wise 词族还给出 likewise 与 clockwise，两者都指做事或行进的方式。

normal.en: Otherwise known as is the fixed phrase for a second name, and or otherwise pairs with or to cover remaining cases.
normal.cn: otherwise known as 是表示「另一个名字」的固定说法，而 or otherwise 与 or 连用，覆盖剩下的情况。

normal.en: As a conjunction it joins two clauses: do this, otherwise that will happen, which is why it often sits mid-sentence.
normal.cn: 作连词时它连接两个分句：做这个，否则就会那样，所以它常出现在句子中间。

abstract.en: A word that means in other ways quietly admits that every choice closes off another path.
abstract.cn: 一个意为「以别的方式」的词，默默承认每个选择都关上了另一条路。

abstract.en: The second name of a place or person is often hidden behind otherwise known as, a phrase doing the work of a footnote.
abstract.cn: 一个地方或一个人的第二个名字，常常藏在 otherwise known as 后面，这个短语干着脚注的活。

abstract.en: To say a thing is fine otherwise is to hold the good and the bad in one short sentence.
abstract.cn: 说一件东西除此之外都不错，就是用一句很短的话同时握住好与坏。

examples.en: You should leave now, otherwise you will miss the last train.
examples.cn: 你现在就该走，否则会错过末班车。

examples.en: The room is small but otherwise comfortable.
examples.cn: 这个房间虽小，其他方面却舒适。

examples.en: There was no choice; he could not have acted otherwise.
examples.cn: 当时别无选择，他不可能有别的做法。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德外兹」——阿德偏向外面走，另选了一条路；记住 otherwise 是否则、以别的方式。

root: 由古英语短语 on oþre wisan（以别的方式）凝固成一个词，其中 oþer 意为「另一个」，wīse 意为「方式」；这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

sensesIntro.en: The core is another way; the senses divide by a condition, by other respects, and by the plain sense of doing something differently.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「另一种方式」；义项按假设的条件、其他方面，以及「以不同方式做事」的本义分出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a road forking at a signpost, one board fallen flat while the other path stands almost unused.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条路在岔口分成两支，一块木牌倒在左边，指向右边的那条路几乎没人走过。

branches.en: a platform after the last train has gone
branches.cn: 末班车开走后的站台

branches.en: a small room that is pleasant in every other way
branches.cn: 除面积之外都让人满意的一间小屋

branches.en: a path that could have been taken instead
branches.cn: 本可以改走的那一条路

branches.en: the same word for a condition and an alternative
branches.cn: 同一个词，既表示条件，也表示另一种选择

branches.en: other respects and other ways belong to one phrase
branches.cn: 「其他方面」与「别的方式」出自同一个短语

intro.en: The word is a frozen Old English phrase made of the adjective for other and the noun for manner, now written together as one adverb.
intro.cn: 这个词是一句凝固的古英语短语，由表示「别的」的形容词与表示「方式」的名词组成，如今合写成一个副词。

latinIntro.en: Otherwise is built entirely from Old English words, and no reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this compound.
latinIntro.cn: otherwise 完全由古英语词构成，这个复合词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: in the direction of a clock

definition_zh: 负荷；载荷；载重；负担；装载；加载
definition_en: the weight or force carried by a structure, vehicle or machine, or to put goods, data or a charge into something
core_image: 吊车把一卷钢带挂上吊钩，仪表指针逼近额定值，司机抬手示意停止起升
scene: 吊车把钢卷挂上吊钩，仪表指针逼近额定值，司机抬手示意停止起升。 The crane stopped because the load exceeded its rated limit.
sceneCN: 这里指吊具承受的重量（第 1 个义项：结构或吊具承受的载荷）；句意为吊车停了下来，因为载荷超过了额定限度。图中可辨识物件：吊钩、钢卷、载荷仪表、司机、警戒线；对应第 1 个义项。

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加表示施动者的名词尾构成，义为「装料机；装载者」
由该动词加已然词尾构成，义为「载重的；有负载的」
由该动词加表示进行的名词尾构成，义为「装载；加载」
由表示「超过」的前缀加该词构成，义为「超载」
由表示「取消」的前缀加该动词构成，义为「卸载」

senses.title: The weight a structure carries
senses.definition: the force or weight that a structure, lifting device or machine has to bear
senses.definitionCN: 结构、吊具或机器必须承受的力或重量
senses.example: The beam is designed for a load of ten tonnes.
senses.exampleCN: 这根梁按十吨载荷设计。
senses.why: The word began as a way or a carrying, and engineering fixed it to the weight being carried.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指「路途、承载」，工程语境把它固定到被承载的重量上。

senses.title: The capacity of a vehicle
senses.definition: the amount of goods or weight that a vehicle or vessel is able to carry
senses.definitionCN: 车辆或船舶能够装载的货物量或重量
senses.example: The truck took a full load of gravel.
senses.exampleCN: 卡车装了一整载碎石。
senses.why: A carrying word naturally measures how much can be carried at once.
senses.whyCN: 表示「承载」的词自然用来度量一次能带多少。

senses.title: The weight of work
senses.definition: the amount of work or responsibility a person or system must deal with
senses.definitionCN: 一个人或系统必须处理的工作量或责任
senses.example: The new clerk cut the load on the front desk.
senses.exampleCN: 新来的职员减轻了前台的负担。
senses.why: Work is imagined as goods to be carried, and an extra person shares the load.
senses.whyCN: 工作被想象成要搬运的货物，多一个人就分担了荷载。

senses.title: The demand on a circuit
senses.definition: the power or current drawn by a device or system from a supply
senses.definitionCN: 设备或系统从电源取用的功率或电流
senses.example: The generator tripped when the load doubled.
senses.exampleCN: 负载翻倍时发电机跳闸了。
senses.why: Electrical demand behaves like a weight on a supply, and the old word fitted without change.
senses.whyCN: 用电需求像压在电源上的重量，老词原样就用上了。

senses.title: To put goods on board
senses.definition: to put goods, fuel or material onto a vehicle or into a container
senses.definitionCN: 把货物、燃料或材料放上车船或容器
senses.example: They load the pallets before sunrise.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在日出前把托盘装好。
senses.why: The noun of a burden turned into the verb of placing it, a common British pairing.
senses.whyCN: 「负担」的名词转成「放置负担」的动词，这是英语里常见的名词动化。

senses.title: To charge a weapon or device
senses.definition: to put a charge, film or medium into a weapon, camera or appliance
senses.definitionCN: 把弹药、胶片或介质装入武器、相机或器具
senses.example: He loaded the camera with a fresh roll.
senses.exampleCN: 他给相机装上一卷新胶卷。
senses.why: A device also carries something and needs to be filled before it works.
senses.whyCN: 装置同样要承载东西，用之前必须先填满。

senses.title: To bring data into memory
senses.definition: to transfer a file or program into a computer's memory so that it can be used
senses.definitionCN: 把文件或程序传入计算机内存以便使用
senses.example: The program will load the map on startup.
senses.exampleCN: 程序启动时会加载这张地图。
senses.why: Computing reused the idea of putting something into a carrier before it can act.
senses.whyCN: 计算机沿用「先装进载体才能运作」这个思路。

senses.title: An emotional burden
senses.definition: a weight of worry or responsibility that a person feels
senses.definitionCN: 一个人感受到的忧虑或责任之重
senses.example: She carried a heavy load after the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 事故之后她背负着沉重的心理负担。
senses.why: The body carries weight and the mind borrows the same measure.
senses.whyCN: 身体承担重量，心智借用了同一套度量。

senses.title: The demand on an engine
senses.definition: the amount of power an engine or motor must produce at a given moment
senses.definitionCN: 发动机或电动机在某一时刻必须输出的功率
senses.example: At full load the engine runs at its hottest.
senses.exampleCN: 满负荷时发动机温度最高。
senses.why: Every machine has a working demand, and engineers call that demand its load.
senses.whyCN: 每台机器都有运转需求，工程师把这个需求称作它的负荷。

intro.en: Load goes back to Old English lad, a way or a course, from the reconstructed Proto-Germanic laidō, to go forth. The sense of something carried appeared in Middle English, and the verb followed.
intro.cn: 这个词可追到古英语 lad「路途、进程」，来自原始日耳曼语的重构形式 laidō「向前走」。表示「被承载之物」的意思在中古英语出现，动词随后产生。

items.en: Lad meant a way, a course or a journey, and the earliest sense was about travelling rather than weight.
items.cn: 这个词意为路途、进程或旅程，最早的意思与行走有关，而非重量。

items.en: The Proto-Germanic noun meant a way or a leading, and related forms in other Germanic languages also mean a road or a track.
items.cn: 原始日耳曼语名词意为路途或引导，其他日耳曼语中的相关形式也指道路或轨迹。

items.en: By the thirteenth century the word also named what a person or animal carried, and the meaning moved from route to burden; how that shift came about is source uncertain, and one hypothesis links it to a related verb meaning to lead.
items.cn: 到十三世纪，这个词也指人或牲畜背负的东西，意思从路线转向负担；这一语义转变的来源不确定，另有假说认为它受表示「引导、带领」的同族动词影响。

items.en: The verb to put a load on appeared in the fourteenth century, and to load a gun or camera followed later.
items.cn: 表示「给……装货」的动词在十四世纪出现，给枪炮或相机装填的用法随后产生。

items.en: Structural and mechanical engineering gave the noun its precise force sense, and its first attestation date is uncertain.
items.cn: 结构与机械工程赋予这个名词精确的力学含义，首见年代不确定。

items.en: The nineteenth century applied the word to circuits, and the twentieth to data and programs.
items.cn: 十九世纪把它用于电路，二十世纪又用于数据与程序。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like load; the second group names neighbouring ideas of weight and filling.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与「load」相近；第二组是与「重量、装载」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: A machine or person that loads material, or a program that loads files.
entries.definitionCN: 指装料的机器或人，也指加载文件的程序。

entries.definition: Carrying a load, or charged with something.
entries.definitionCN: 指载着负荷的，或装填了东西的。

entries.definition: To put more weight or demand on something than it can bear.
entries.definitionCN: 指给某物加上超过其承受能力的重量或需求。

entries.definition: To take goods off a vehicle or remove a burden.
entries.definitionCN: 指把货物从车上卸下或卸去负担。

entries.definition: A vein of ore; it sounds identical but comes from a word for a way or a lead.
entries.definitionCN: 指矿脉；发音相同，但来自表示「路径、引导」的词。

entries.definition: A heavy load, especially one that is hard to carry or bear.
entries.definitionCN: 指沉重的负荷，尤指难以承担的重负。

entries.definition: The heaviness of an object, or a mass placed on something.
entries.definitionCN: 指物体的重量，或放在某物上的质量。

entries.definition: Goods carried by a ship, aircraft or truck.
entries.definitionCN: 指船、飞机或卡车运载的货物。

entries.definition: The part of a vehicle's load that earns revenue or does the work.
entries.definitionCN: 指载具负荷中产生收益或执行任务的那部分。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real way-word origin, the real trade family and real engineering phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「路途」来源、真实行业同族词与真实工程搭配。

normal.en: Load first meant a road, then the thing a road carries.
normal.cn: load 最初指一条路，后来指这条路所承载的东西。

normal.en: Load capacity and heavy load are the engineering phrases.
normal.cn: 承载能力与重载是工程里的说法。

normal.en: Load a truck, load a camera and load data are three filling acts.
normal.cn: 装车、装胶卷与加载数据是三个「装填」动作。

normal.en: Overload and unload mark too much and none at all.
normal.cn: 超载与卸载标出「太多」与「一点不剩」。

normal.en: Workload is the same weight carried by a person rather than a beam.
normal.cn: 工作量就是由人而不是梁来承担的同一份重量。

abstract.en: A load is a promise the structure must keep every second.
abstract.cn: 载荷是结构每一秒都必须守住的承诺。

abstract.en: The same word weighs a steel coil and a bad memory.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既称钢卷的重量，也称一段坏记忆的重量。

abstract.en: Loading is putting something in so that the thing can begin.
abstract.cn: 加载就是把东西放进去，好让那件事得以开始。

examples.en: The column carries the load of the roof above it.
examples.cn: 这根柱子承受上方屋顶的载荷。

examples.en: Workers load the truck before the gate opens.
examples.cn: 工人在大门打开前装车。

examples.en: The screen froze while the program was loading the file.
examples.cn: 程序加载文件时屏幕卡住了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「漏德」——压在梁上的重量不能「漏」掉，得全「德」扛住：负荷

root: 古英语 lad「路途、进程」← 原始日耳曼语 laidō「向前走」；同族形式多指道路或轨迹。十三世纪起转指所背负之物，十四世纪产生动词，十五世纪用于枪炮装填，十九世纪用于电路，二十世纪用于数据；力学义的确切年代来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses all concern what is carried: force on a structure, goods in a vehicle, work on a person, current in a circuit, cargo placed on board, a charge in a device, data in memory, worry in a mind, and power drawn from an engine.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都与「承载」有关：结构受力、车辆载货、人的工作量、电路电流、装船装车、装置装填、内存数据、心中忧虑与发动机输出功率。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hook lifts a coil until the gauge reaches the rated limit.
core.cn: 核心意象：吊钩吊起钢卷，直到仪表到达额定极限。

branches.en: THE FORCE ON A MACHINE: a beam bearing tonnes, and an engine working at full demand.
branches.cn: 机器所受的力：梁承受数吨重量，发动机满负荷运转。

branches.en: THE CARGO: the amount a vehicle can take, and the act of putting it aboard.
branches.cn: 货物：车辆能装的数量，以及把货装上去的动作。

branches.en: THE HUMAN WEIGHT: too much work at a desk, and too much worry in a mind.
branches.cn: 人的重量：桌上过多的工作，与心中过多的忧虑。

branches.en: THE ELECTRICAL DRAW: current taken from a supply until the breaker trips.
branches.cn: 电的取用：从电源取用电流，直到断路器跳闸。

branches.en: THE THING PUT IN: a charge in a weapon, and a file brought into memory.
branches.cn: 装进去的东西：装进武器的弹药，以及带进内存的文件。

intro.en: Load is a native English word of Germanic origin, so it has no Latin ancestor; its Latin list is left empty.
intro.cn: 这是一个日耳曼来源的英语本族词，没有拉丁语祖先，因此拉丁词条留空。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source for load; the relevant origin is Proto-Germanic laidō, a word for a way or a course.
latinIntro.cn: load 没有拉丁语来源；相关来源是原始日耳曼语 laidō，指路途或进程。

items.example: The oldest sense is about moving, not carrying.
items.exampleCN: 最古老的意思关乎行走，而非承载。

items.example: The form is reconstructed from related languages.
items.exampleCN: 该形式由相关语言重构而来。

items.example: The compound moves the load from steel to people.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词把负荷从钢梁转到人身上。

items.meaning: the earning part of a load
items.meaningCN: 负荷中产生收益的部分
items.example: The compound separates cargo from the vehicle.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词把货物与载具分开。

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加表示施动者的名词尾构成，义为「装载机；装载者」
由该动词加表示进行的名词尾构成，义为「装载；加载」

由表示「反向」的前缀加该动词构成，义为「卸载」
由「工作」加该名词构成，义为「工作量」

definition_zh: 块；团；肿块；把……归并；勉强接受
definition_en: a solid mass with no regular shape, a swelling on the body, to group separate things into one mass, or to accept something unpleasant because there is no other choice
core_image: 一块从煤堆里滚落的黑块，棱角不平，落在掌心沉甸甸的
scene: 厨房台面上放着一袋刚买回来的方糖，其中几块粘成了不规则的一团。 He dropped a lump of sugar into the hot tea and watched it sink.
sceneCN: 这里 lump 是「块、团」（第 1 个义项：无定形的固体块）；句意为他往热茶里丢了一块方糖，看着它沉下去。图中可辨识物件：厨房台面、方糖袋、茶杯。

collocations.zh: 接受也得接受，不接受也得接受

derivatives.zh: 由 lump 加 -y 构成，义为「结块的；疙疙瘩瘩的」
由 lump 加 -ish 构成，义为「笨重的；迟钝的」

senses.title: A solid mass with no regular shape
senses.definition: a piece of solid material that has no regular shape and is felt as one heavy mass
senses.definitionCN: 一块没有规则形状、被感知为一整个沉重整体的固体
senses.example: He dropped a lump of sugar into the hot tea.
senses.exampleCN: 他往热茶里丢了一块方糖。
senses.why: The word starts from what the hand feels: a portion of material that has set or been pressed into one body, with no edges worth counting.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从手的触感出发：一部分材料凝成或压成了一整块，边上没有值得去数的棱角。

senses.title: A swelling under the skin
senses.definition: an area of the body that has risen into a hard or rounded swelling
senses.definitionCN: 身体上隆起的一块硬或圆形的肿大部位
senses.example: She found a small lump on her arm and had it checked.
senses.exampleCN: 她发现手臂上有个小肿块，就去做了检查。
senses.why: A swelling has the same outline as a mass of clay or coal, so the body borrows the word for anything that pushes up under the skin.
senses.whyCN: 肿块与一团黏土或煤块的轮廓相同，于是身体借用了这个词，指任何在皮下顶起来的东西。

senses.title: To group things into one mass
senses.definition: to put separate people or things into one group without sorting them
senses.definitionCN: 把分开的人或物不加区分地放进同一组
senses.example: The report lumps all the small shops together as one category.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告把所有小店归并成同一类。
senses.why: If separate pieces are thrown into one pile, their edges disappear into a single mass; the verb is that throwing, applied to facts and categories.
senses.whyCN: 如果把分开的块丢进同一堆，它们的边就消失在一整团里；动词就是这一「丢」，只是对象换成了事实与类别。

senses.title: To accept something unpleasant
senses.definition: to swallow an unpleasant situation because it cannot be changed
senses.definitionCN: 因为无法改变而把不愉快的处境硬吞下去
senses.example: He did not like the decision, but he had to lump it.
senses.exampleCN: 他不喜欢这个决定，但也只能忍着接受。
senses.why: The phrase like it or lump it pictures the bad news as one hard lump that must be swallowed whole, since there is no way to chew it into smaller pieces.
senses.whyCN: like it or lump it 把坏消息想成一整块硬东西：既然没法嚼碎，就只能整块吞下。

intro.en: Lump is a Middle English noun for a shapeless mass; its deeper origin is uncertain, and the verb and medical senses grew from that solid block.
intro.cn: lump 是中古英语中表示「无定形一块」的名词；它更早的来源不确定，动词义与医学义都是从这块固体生长出来的。

items.en: The noun lump, also written lompe, first names a shapeless mass of material, neither shaped nor measured.
items.cn: 名词 lump 也写作 lompe，最初指一块既无形状也无定量的材料。

items.en: A common suggestion compares Middle Dutch lomp, a rag or a clumsy piece, and German Lumpen, a rag; the comparison is offered as possible, not as settled.
items.cn: 一种常见说法把它与中古荷兰语 lomp（破布、笨重的一块）和德语 Lumpen（破布）相比较；这只是一条可能的线索，并非定论。

items.en: The verb appears with the sense of throwing separate things into one mass, which gives phrases such as lump together and later lump sum.
items.cn: 动词义出现，意思是把分开的东西丢成一整堆，由此产生 lump together 以及后来的 lump sum 等说法。

items.en: Medical writers use lump for a swelling felt under the skin, and the same outline produces the phrase a lump in the throat for strong emotion.
items.cn: 医学作者用 lump 指皮下摸到的肿块；同样的轮廓又产生 a lump in the throat 这一说法，用来形容情绪激动。

items.en: Phrases such as take one's lumps and like it or lump it keep the sense of a hard thing that simply has to be borne.
items.cn: take one's lumps 与 like it or lump it 之类的说法，保留了「一块硬东西只能硬扛」的含义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms and derivatives built on lump; the near-meaning group gathers words for masses, pieces and swellings.
note.cn: 形近组收由 lump 构成的变形与派生词；近义组收表示块状物、团块与肿起的词。

entries.definition: Full of lumps, or uneven in texture.
entries.definitionCN: 由 lump 加 -y 构成，义为「结块的；疙疙瘩瘩的」。

entries.definition: Heavy, awkward and slow in shape or manner.
entries.definitionCN: 由 lump 加 -ish 构成，义为「笨重的；迟钝的」。

entries.definition: More than one lump.
entries.definitionCN: lump 的复数形式，指多块。

entries.definition: One single payment of money instead of several.
entries.definitionCN: 由 lump 与 sum 复合，义为「一次性整付的总额」。

entries.definition: A thick, solid piece of something.
entries.definitionCN: 厚实的一块；多指从大块上切下的一块。

entries.definition: A solid piece with flat sides, often rectangular.
entries.definitionCN: 块；常指有平面、近似方形的固体。

entries.definition: A large amount of material with no clear shape.
entries.definitionCN: 一大团；强调整体而不强调边缘。

entries.definition: A place on the body that has become larger and rounder.
entries.definitionCN: 肿起；医学语境中比 lump 更中性的说法。

normalIntro.en: The word begins as the name of a shapeless mass, and its family keeps returning to hard pieces, swellings and things thrown into one pile.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词起初是一团无定形材料的名字，同族词反复回到硬块、肿起以及被丢成一堆的东西。

normal.en: Lump is first a noun for a shapeless mass; the verb comes later and means to throw separate things into one pile.
normal.cn: lump 首先是名词，指无定形的一团；动词义较晚出现，意思是把分开的东西丢成一堆。

normal.en: Lump together keeps that picture: separate pieces lose their edges once they are dropped into the same heap.
normal.cn: lump together 保留了这个画面：分开的块一旦被丢进同一堆，就失去了各自的边。

normal.en: A lump of sugar is a small pressed block, which shows how loose the word is about exact shape.
normal.cn: 一块方糖就是压成的小方块，可见这个词对具体形状并不严格。

normal.en: A lump on the arm is a swelling shaped like a mass under the skin, so the medical sense borrows the physical one.
normal.cn: 手臂上的肿块就是皮下形似一团的东西，医学义直接借用了物理义。

normal.en: Like it or lump it means swallow the bad news whole, as if it were one hard lump with no way to chew it.
normal.cn: like it or lump it 意为把坏消息整块吞下，好像那是一块没法嚼的硬东西。

abstract.en: A lump has no edges to hold, which is why the word suits anything we cannot easily take apart.
abstract.cn: 一块 lump 没有可抓的棱角，所以这个词适合形容任何我们难以拆开的东西。

abstract.en: To lump people together is to lose the outlines that made them separate, and that is exactly the harm the verb describes.
abstract.cn: 把人 lump together，就是丢掉让他们彼此分开的轮廓，而这正是这个动词所指的害处。

abstract.en: A hard lump can be swallowed but not digested, which is a fair picture of a truth we accept without liking.
abstract.cn: 硬块吞得下却消化不了，这正好形容我们接受却并不喜欢的真相。

examples.en: He dropped a lump of sugar into the hot tea.
examples.cn: 他往热茶里丢了一块方糖。

examples.en: The report lumps all the small shops together as one category.
examples.cn: 这份报告把所有小店归并成同一类。

examples.en: He did not like the decision, but he had to lump it.
examples.cn: 他不喜欢这个决定，但也只能忍着接受。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「隆噗」——一块东西落到桌面，闷闷一声；lump 就是块、团。

root: 中古英语 lump（也写作 lompe）指无定形的一块；来源不确定，一般认为可能与中古荷兰语 lomp（破布、笨重的一块）或德语 Lumpen（破布）有关，但没有定论，也没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is one solid mass; the senses divide into the mass itself, the swelling on the body, the act of throwing things into a pile, and the act of swallowing an unpleasant thing whole.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一整块固体；义项由此分出块状物本身、身上的肿起、把东西丢成一堆的动作，以及把不快整块吞下的态度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a black block rolling off a coal heap, its edges rough, heavy in the palm.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块从煤堆里滚落的黑块，棱角不平，落在掌心沉甸甸的。

branches.en: a black block rolling off a coal heap
branches.cn: 从煤堆上滚落的一块黑煤

branches.en: a sugar cube dissolving at the bottom of a cup
branches.cn: 杯底慢慢化开的方糖

branches.en: a swelling rising under the skin
branches.cn: 皮肤下鼓起的一块肿

branches.en: odds and ends pushed into one pile
branches.cn: 零碎东西被推成一堆

branches.en: a man swallowing a bitter answer

intro.en: The word is a Middle English noun of uncertain origin; its English family is built with two suffixes and the ordinary verb forms.
intro.cn: 这个词是中古英语名词，来源不确定；它在英语里的同族词由两个后缀与常规动词形式构成。

latinIntro.en: Lump has no reliable Latin source; its origin is uncertain and is usually discussed through Dutch or German words, so no Latin family is listed.
latinIntro.cn: lump 没有可靠的拉丁语来源；它的来源不确定，通常在荷兰语或德语词里讨论，因此不列拉丁同族词。

items.example: The soup still had lumps in it.

items.meaning: grouped or accepted in the past
items.example: They lumped the two bills together.
items.exampleCN: 他们把两张账单合在一起。

items.meaning: the act of grouping things in one mass
items.meaningCN: 把东西归并成一堆的行为
items.example: Lumping all the cases together hides the differences.
items.exampleCN: 把所有情况归并在一起会掩盖差异。

items.meaningCN: 由名词构成形容词的后缀

items.meaning: full of lumps or uneven in texture

items.meaningCN: 构成表示性质的形容词后缀

items.example: The old chair was lumpish but solid.
items.exampleCN: 这把旧椅子笨重但结实。
